subject: TAKE ACTION: Protect the Western Arctic from Trump’s Attacks
body:
Help us reach 5,000 signatures before the August 4 deadline.

If you are unable to see the message below, [click here to view](https://links.messages.lcv.org/servlet/MailView?ms=MTI3NDI4MjIS1&r=NjA3MDU0MTAzNTc3S0&j=MjI2MDI4MTM3MgS2&mt=1&rt=0).

## **Take Action to Protect the Western Arctic**
**from Trump’s Attacks**

The Trump administration is moving to revoke protections for the Western Arctic, one of the most ecologically important landscapes in the world. We need your help: There's a short window when the Interior Department must collect feedback. _It's crucial that environmentalists make their voices heard before the deadline. _ [**_ Please take action right now — it only takes a moment to help us reach our 5,000 signature goal >>_**](https://links.messages.lcv.)
---
| | | [ TAKE ACTION ](https://links.messages.lcv.org/els/v2/G8bxcKr2r_)
---
| | | | Peter — The Trump administration is proposing to roll back publicly supported protections in the Western Arctic, one of the most ecologically important landscapes on Earth, and allow Big Oil companies to start destructive drilling operations. The Western Arctic is home to polar bears, wolves, moose, America’s largest caribou herds, and nesting birds from around the world. The landscape is also crucial to the culture and traditions of Alaska Natives, and helps fight the effects of climate change by reducing greenhouse gases from the air. Now through August 4, the Interior Department must collect feedback on their proposed protection rollback. **We need your help, Peter** : We’ve set a goal to submit 5,000 comments from LCV members like you. Please act now — _it only takes a moment to add your name. _
---
| | [**_Help ensure that environmentalists’ voices are heard before the August 4 deadline. Help us reach 5,000 signatures demanding that the Trump administration maintain protections for the Western Arctic >>_**](https://links.messages.lcv.)
---
| | | [ TAKE ACTION ](https://links.messages.lcv.org/els/v2/w_)
---
| | Trump’s proposal puts the interests of Big Oil above those of local communities and the American people, opening up 13 million acres of land to oil and gas development by striking down Special Areas protections for many of the Western Arctic’s unique landscapes. With rapid changes from climate change and continued threats from oil and gas development, **it is critical that we make sure the Trump administration hears from the public that they must maintain strong protections for vulnerable areas in the Western Arctic.** The oil industry wants to roll back protections in the Western Arctic — even when the price is sacrificing sensitive ecosystems and impacting cultural resources for Indigenous communities. _Our movement needs to respond. _
---
| | [**_Make your voice heard: Please don’t wait — take action now and help us reach 5,000 signatures demanding Trump maintain protections for the Western Arctic >>_**](https://links.messages.lcv.)
---
| | Thanks for taking action, Peter.
---
| | America Fitzpatrick
Conservation Program Director
League of Conservation Voters

Wisconsin has been at the center of our work since we launched the NDRC. From the start, it was abundantly clear that the state was governed by illegitimate minority rule.
For more than a decade, conservatives held control of the Supreme Court, while Republican Governor Scott Walker and his allies had egregiously gerrymandered the state legislature to create artificially large GOP majorities in spite of growing support for Democrats across the state.
**But the people of Wisconsin didn’t let those extreme tactics happen without a fight, and the NDRC joined them in a relentless effort to bring fairness back to the state.** In the last two years, we’ve been able to help re-elect Democratic Governor Tony Evers and finally flip the majority of the state supreme court. And thanks to those tireless efforts, new, fair legislative maps are now in place, creating a path to win majorities in 2026.
**We’ve seen what’s possible in Wisconsin, and now, it’s on us to fight across the country. **Over the next two years, we’re investing in critical elections that will shape the future of fair maps across at least 13 states. By electing pro-democracy champions at the state level in 2025 and 2026, we can prevent mid-decade gerrymandering and build a foundation for fair and independent redistricting following the release of the 2030 Census data.
[**Fighting gerrymandering and nefarious anti-democracy efforts requires consistent investment over the short and long term. Will you donate to the NDRC today and fuel these efforts to create a democracy that’s representative of all Americans?**](https://click.everyaction.com/k/112077473/559343942/-246980373?refcode=don_ndrc_tier1_email_WISupremeCourtAbortion_email_202050724-NDRC-Tier1-WISupremeCourtAbortion_&utm_source=email&utm_medium=email&utm_term=don&utm_content=202050724-NDRC-Tier1-WISupremeCourtAbortion_&utm_campaign=WISupremeCourtAbortion&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9FQS9FQTAxMy8xLzg5Mjk0IiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogIjI3YTgxOTRjLWVhNjgtZjAxMS04ZGM5LTYwNDViZGE5ZDk2YiIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=oj4ellKoVWLS4E6mWmYHgHSEDwd1N0HmE3Ew6pvJoLI=)

Atlanta Voice: Georgia seeks another Supreme Court showdown over Voting Rights Act
Bad news for everyone, Team: The state of Georgia is seeking another Supreme Court showdown over the Voting Rights Act, asking a federal appeals court to interpret the 1965 law in a way that could make it much harder to prove minority votes have been illegally diluted.
Georgia is trying persuade the judges to make up a new, harder-to-prove standard that could hobble Voting Rights Act lawsuits, less than two years after the U.S. Supreme Court turned back a separate challenge from Alabama to the VRA.
From the AP: " A lawyer for the state asked a three-judge panel of the 11th Circuit U.S. Court of Appeals in Atlanta to overturn a lower court that required lawmakers to draw more Black-majority electoral districts. Georgia’s Republican Secretary of State Brad Raffensperger argued in court filings that the Voting Rights Act is being misused to bolster Democratic election chances and that white voters prefer Republicans for nonracial reasons. "

| | It wasn't enough for Republicans to gut people's health care and food assistance when they passed their budget bill. Last week, they added insult to injury by _defunding public broadcasting – including NPR and PBS._ This cuts millions of children's access to free educational programs. It will leave news deserts, particularly in rural areas of Oregon and the country, at a time when smaller newspapers and news outlets are being forced to close their doors over a lack of funding. And public broadcasting isn't only a source of trusted information and news. It also serves as the primary emergency alert system for many rural areas of the country, including my home state. Defunding public alert systems for severe weather like wildfires or floods, after what happened in Texas earlier this month, is unthinkably dangerous. It's yet another attack by Trump and his allies on the free press. (When you know you can't win a debate on the policy merits, why not just rig the information game?) It makes it harder for people to get fair and accurate reporting about their political leaders. **I'm outraged about these latest Republican cuts. They will be a wrecking ball to public information and news in rural Oregon and the rest of the country.** **Everything Republicans have done since gaining their trifecta of power will make our families and communities less safe.** Having easy access to basic information and news shouldn't be a political football. clean_body: But Republicans are desperate to rig the information game. | | | | It wasn't enough for Republicans to gut people's health care and food assistance when they passed their budget bill. Last week, they added insult to injury by defunding public broadcasting – including NPR and PBS. This cuts millions of children's access to free educational programs. It will leave news deserts, particularly in rural areas of Oregon and the country, at a time when smaller newspapers and news outlets are being forced to close their doors over a lack of funding. And public broadcasting isn't only a source of trusted information and news. It also serves as the primary emergency alert system for many rural areas of the country, including my home state. Defunding public alert systems for severe weather like wildfires or floods, after what happened in Texas earlier this month, is unthinkably dangerous. It's yet another attack by Trump and his allies on the free press. (When you know you can't win a debate on the policy merits, why not just rig the information game?) It makes it harder for people to get fair and accurate reporting about their political leaders. I'm outraged about these latest Republican cuts. They will be a wrecking ball to public information and news in rural Oregon and the rest of the country. Everything Republicans have done since gaining their trifecta of power will make our families and communities less safe. Having easy access to basic information and news shouldn't be a political football. I'm going to keep fighting to ensure that folks remain informed. And I'll keep fighting to elect a Congress that reverses these harmful cuts. body:

| [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/112078724/559376041/-1860252395?refcode=-header-&amount=25&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMjQvMS8xMDMxMTgiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiMTVjY2NkYWQtZjI2OC1mMDExLThkYzktNjA0NWJkYTlkOTZiIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=8688d9GXCWyCQFARAwmb2ghf_aaX4Gccol29ZKZFPzE=) | Peter, This is bad: Kevin Lincoln just announced his campaign to unseat Josh Harder. [_**We’re going to explain why this guy is so scary... but first, we need you to send in a critical donation to help us fight back right away!**_](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/112078725/559376042/-1149165536?&refcode=E14274-20250723-ScaryOpponent-SL-CampaignNews&amount=5&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMjQvMS8xMDMxMTgiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiMTVjY2NkYWQtZjI2OC1mMDExLThkYzktNjA0NWJkYTlkOTZiIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=8688d9GXCWyCQFARAwmb2ghf_aaX4Gccol29ZKZFPzE=) _**[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/112078726/559376043/-1149165536?&refcode=E14274-20250723-ScaryOpponent-Image-CampaignNews&amount=5&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMjQvMS8xMDMxMTgiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiMTVjY2NkYWQtZjI2OC1mMDExLThkYzktNjA0NWJkYTlkOTZiIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=8688d9GXCWyCQFARAwmb2ghf_aaX4Gccol29ZKZFPzE=)**_ If the name Kevin Lincoln sounds familiar, it should. He came within just 4 points of flipping this seat red, and now he’s back with even more money, power, and GOP support behind him. body:
[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/112079139/559385905/-2113420158?source=EM_NBI_JP_20250724_FR_Monarch_0_6MD_Jimmy_NA_NA_Butterflies&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTIvMS85MTkwMSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJlZWNjZmEwOS1mYzY4LWYwMTEtOGRjOS02MDQ1YmRhOWQ5NmIiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=UQTqxH15W7CJUl1z_dtIiqUASKHxu9uyMvaLSIghuRE=&emci=e9ccfa09-fc68-f011-8dc9-6045bda9d96b&emdi=eeccfa09-fc68-f011-8dc9-6045bda9d96b&ceid=6108787) | Peter,

Since the 1980s, the western monarch butterfly has **_lost 99% of its population_**. That’s bad, very bad. Monarchs are vital pollinators that support our food systems, biodiversity, and the natural beauty of places like California’s Central Coast.

That’s why I authored and reintroduced the **MONARCH Act**. It invests **_$12.5 million_** each year into restoring monarch habitat, funding conservation research, and protecting pollinators that sustain our environment and economy.

| Why compassion is a failed narrative for Democrats
Firstly, please note that this writer is a supporter of Democratic values, which are not necessarily the bastion of Democrats. They are the foundation on which this great nation stands through good and bad times. They are indelible and inalienable. I am also not writing that compassion should be abandoned. Definitely not. What I am writing is that the narrative of compassion does not impact the voter base, especially the far right, as the Democrats expect. They have been pounding this drum of morality and compassion for so very long, and it continues to have a lesser and lesser effect on voter behavior.
---
| |
---
| Does this mean that we should also give up on compassion and outrage over the injustices that surround us? Absolutely not. But we must stop just listening and start hearing what registers with people.
We live in a country where the majority of people who voted did so for a felon, sexual molester, corrupt politician, corrupt businessperson, and textbook megalomaniac, and still they cry for more. In fact, the majority of Americans prefer an authoritarian government to a democracy. ([USNews](https://zmhksxhbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001HXwBAkfVnLJpFnOgMFoGtbGlWxqQBPU57FqHpsdMyn033j4ZdIePJ8JFQCumbzdGmZxCdn5PWEWSgpoYkz6T78CkopZsOV8h_zuNuLlKk8biysXcZ5ZM6pIq_TQlNmaoZ5BonaGdhwhizTSB3dIUVSXm8Rkp8np5vzza_TC7b7Kc9YHSB_UK1a6_9UCIpR1pq38oMqzI8BcVxOWuyshvJOKmqQb6pr1TOlRgQWrSroE_ZoRfpe3TVYaD7FN6vozIBbWbo16hKC9GnxB4v8tYcLfSPzajEpyMrR6LFoIVcUZORifnAF9J4u8sI-NojxBb&c=A45RVOzI4cAOaMv5tfyc6qNNeB9PU4WFki8o1HYLJ4lnedkKL0_sXg==&ch=OQTADItEctOrBcLLpairaZhVe_FUdrac_I8ldWTCktQ_oTvcB97-jw==))
Why is it that compassion and morality are no longer the emotional levers they once were? I do not know. We live in a world that is a constant bombardment of negative emotions, and it may be nothing more than a self protective defense mechanism. Or more likely, part of a much more complex environment of the evil that men do, the constant threat of violence, being led by a corrupt government, and fed a steady diet of lies. All of this could fall under the heading of surviving rather than thriving and may be driving a very "me right now" sense of protectionism. We also know that the far right has for decades been successful in vilifying the poor and underprivileged to the point that it is an accepted truth among several generations of voters.
---
| |
---
| Regardless, it is real, and we must learn to speak to it. Imagine how foreign the MAGA cries sound to you. That is how our voices sound to them. There is no room for dialogue when ideologies are so far apart.
What would our messaging sound like if we steered away from the heart on our sleeves emotional victim tone that is all too often the voice of Democrats, and started sounding like MAGA, but with our own message?
I did a test using ChatGPT and asked it to write a message using both Democratic and Republican tones and this is what it produced. Democratic: Seventeen million Americans are about to lose their health care. Working families, children, and seniors will be left with nothing. Call your representative now and demand they protect our health, not take it away.
Republican: Seventeen million more people on government health care? That is the plan the left is pushing. Higher taxes, longer wait times, and less freedom. Call your representative and tell them to stop this socialist takeover of your health care.
The Democrat's message is about others. The Republican message is very much about the individual. It is personal. Very personal. There are other contrasts, but this one specifically is important, because in the words of Kevin Sorbo, B actor who played Hercules and MAGA mouthpiece, "Is your freedom more important than my safety? I do not know you. My lunch is more important to me than you are."
Sad as it might be, appealing to one's sense of empathy for others is not working across a wide range of critical voters. Information is skewed, fear is high, and the instinct to protect oneself and family is much greater than empathy for others. This is not bad, because we know that when people feel safe, they open up more to others. It is our responsibility to make that happen. Even if it means that for right now, we must pander to a selfish narrative.
Instead of seventeen million strangers losing Medicaid, it might be about higher local taxes and greater threats of violence in their communities. It is not clear what will work, but we know what has been done. And when the most powerful man in the world can flaunt his corruption as a badge of honor, we know it is not working.
---

These voters are the future of our democracy, but without immediate follow-up, they may be swept up in the fear and falsehoods of the far right.
We will not let that happen.
To fully engage and mobilize these voters before it is too late, we need to raise $75,000 now. Newly registered voters are the most vulnerable and the most promising demographic to reach.
Your donation today keeps our promise to these voters--and to all of us who believe in inclusion, truth, and democracy. Please give now. Every dollar counts.

| Guest Editorial - Allison Murphy Dabler
It is long past time to normalize discussion of, and to put pressure on the DNC and our Democratic Party leadership over its status quo, establishment failures. It has become clear that it is crucial to critique the current Democrats and shed light on how they are hurting the very people they claim to serve by not investing in the younger generation of leaders, and stepping back when they are risking the welfare of this country.
Life expectancy in this country is 79 years of age. When the Big Billionaire Bailout bill was recently passed in the House, sending it to the president's desk, it passed by a 215-214 vote. However, three Democrats were missing. Rep Gerry Connolly (75), had just passed away from cancer the day before. In the few months before that, both representatives Sylvester Turner (70) and Raul Grijalva (77) had passed away and their positions had not yet been filled.
A report from Axios has found that more than half of House Democrats who are 75 and older plan to seek re-election next year, including Rep. Maxine Waters (86), Rep. John Garamendi (80), and Rep. Rosa DeLauro (82). This is an unsustainable and irresponsible model for Democratic success and the future of this country.
Last December, when the DNC was forced to choose who to chair the powerful Oversight Committee, they chose the then 74 year old afore-mentioned Connolly, who had announced his cancer diagnosis just weeks before, over 35 year old Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez. Just this past June, the motivated and hard working David Hogg was pushed out of the DNC, potentially losing Democrats the energized and active youth needed to win elections in the first place.
I'm not one to be ageist, or even call for term limits, but something has to give here. If establishment Democrats refuse to prioritize the recruitment, mentorship, and support of the next generation of leadership, they risk losing the good faith assumption that they can be leaders that will do what is right for the American people, even if it means stepping back. "Leadership is about making others better as a result of your presence, and making sure that impact lasts in your absence." -- Sheryl Sandberg In Solidarity,
Allison Murphy Dabler has held key leadership roles in the Democratic Party, including chairing the Benton County Democrats and co-chairing the State Democratic Platform Committee. She has organized campaigns, boosted voter engagement, and helped build progressive infrastructure across the Tri Cities. In 2025, she was honored with the Norm and Shirley Miller Leadership Award for her service and impact.

## Trump Orders Homeless Removed From Streets
President Trump signed an executive order on Thursday [directing cities and states to remove homeless people](http://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLFugzAQhp_GbI6cM2AzeOjClq4dkYEzuDIY-S5J8_YVkfoE3U466dP_fV-34eZjivvy6Td0HPKw45MSMmMZ1rxhQqIdiXKZsQRPjMQ0gIJGKiOhGWYf02uoq9kFREBdobuaRtfaqqutVgeN1bYZddDW6Nm30Fkz-27qtLUqjF0V3UlTBpqrUm1jLjB2ZoJRoW8hKD-KWuEcOZfLd447rxjSKz-wXKa8VcmtzAcJ_SGgF9DvryMTny8B_QkW0Ctz3rWA_k7y9BPQc7lvh-QsKS67xB-c7hwfKN-eMuQyxX2RfwVkDkH6DUucPEnigsgnpSpuPp4xpUitEbVaNh_Texf_K-bDwW8AAAD__2sAiZI), drug users, and those with serious mental illness from public spaces and place them in treatment centers. It redirects federal funds to support long-term institutional care, prioritizing grants for communities already cracking down on public drug use, camping, and loitering. The directive is framed as a public safety and quality-of-life effort to [restore order in cities](http://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0LGOozAQxvGnMZ0jM5gYChfX0OXaK5GNx2FOBkf2kGzefkWkfYKtR_qPft-_23xzlGi__3UbWo553vFVEzJjmde8YcJad6w1l4AluspYuc6goJfKSOjn4Ci9Z90EGxEBuwZta_pOd4Nqh2a14DG0nde6W0xrhjGCV7GH0YzeB9CmIXvWlIG-Veramwv40SzgFborROW80AoDcS6X_5l2XjGmd35iuSx5a5JdmR9VdH8ETAImXnGllM6bgOkUnCABkwsb7VS5OKa8C5h63Q4GRsnl2B4Sv3A5mJ4oP1L5Y5ehHHd5VJSVCyKfqabY8HhRSlSvRmh13xx9Pjb8qwmfFr4DAAD__6voh9o). According to the White House, more than 274,000 people slept on U.S. streets each night last year.
## Columbia Settles with Feds for $200M
Columbia University agreed to pay [$200 million to the federal government](http://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0L2O6yAUBOCnwV2sw8E2pKC4jbvcdkuLn0NMFpssoFjZp195X2G7kUb6pJmP23IzMcX9_t9spFvIy05HTdQalWXNGyWqdadac_FUgqmNaqsLAo4XkBccF29iei9D53UgQhIdaS5HMQgFXHWrDnxQyMEH4ZTjysqJUF3FyENAgZa6qE8NJI4cYBplj_YqHVogM2EAY9kA5GPLpX_kuLeVQnrnF5Xe5a1Lem3tWZn4x3BmOB_H0Vvrzo7hfI5hOJvSokt0RvelvtPj-Xp_Qu6K9s8jphTrJNkA983E9Ku2P13x0vgTAAD__wBjc1o) to restore research funding cut by the Trump administration over accusations it failed to protect Jewish students during Gaza-related campus protests. The deal [reinstates most of the $400 million](http://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkD2OpDAUhE8DmZF5GNwdONiErDfdEPnnAV75B9mPRn37EaO5wWSfVKpSVf17LS_tg0_bXx1R0ZqXhFcNSIRl2XPEgLUmrDUXh2XVlbBSXYDDyLhkMC5O-_BZROvUigg4tKh6OQ5iePD-0e6ql6s0QljRTxLNwLUbesulQGumJzxk69WdxiWMPefTKDswT2nBcNQTrFybRnB0nnLp_mefaMc1fPIbS2dzbIPaiY7aDH8amBuYr-vqkrH3iltvYL6xgfms7IdsDmc0XjO9FcTKDv1hwDmLPgSfEytYKRdk65mcTxuzJzEqZzyYdtEnX6lo8qzYpAH49JRtUe64bnedZCP4FrUP3-3oV5e-FXwFAAD__1YkjYM) in frozen grants and requires Columbia to adopt stricter campus policies, including protest restrictions and the appointment of an independent monitor. The university denied wrongdoing but called the agreement a step toward stability. Education Secretary Linda McMahon said the settlement sets a “roadmap” for other schools under federal scrutiny.
## Hulk Hogan Dies at 71
Terry Bollea, recognized globally as [pro wrestling legend Hulk Hogan](http://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLGOhCAYhJ9GO8zvL4oWFNfY7bVXGoSflTsEA7hm3_7ivcJ1M5lkMvN9PZaHct6F56faSRYbl0BX9lQKpWWLO3nKOVDOMRlKVuVCueQFAXsGgmG_GOX8e-G1kZYIqatJtqLveDdCO9abnLgaYEJuh9FM1vTDBGg76PgKXOlB107ebSCwbwGGXjS4TkLjCqQGtKDWigMZV2JqvqMLZSPr3_FFqdFxr73cSjly1X1UOFc4X9fVhFXfL-68wvmWFc5xdeVUydFtttP_sC0-VWBXolxuAszpGNgRD6ZPX85EbFcu5KLezDjKTLQs6aAQYUSskzTH5bx3eRAVh-eunP8bVP5F8SXxNwAA__8qEIiJ), died on Thursday in Florida. He was 71. Bollea entered [professional wrestling in the 1970s](http://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLFurDAQAL8GOiNjDIbCxWvo7rUp0d55jZ0s-OR1zuLvo8svpB5pRpqP23aDSPHc_8OBtvi0nViZsBTMW0gHEjKfyJyyw-yBC3LhTUk1CmmEGjcHka5Nt856RIVDi7Y346CHWfZzG-wgQZt5MdM8uN71s1_M7ACc7vWEuJg22rdNGjX2Uk6j6dR9MQ91lwiT8hLujZboYkm5-0zxLAE9XemFuXukoyUbSnlyM_xr1Nqotdba1Ypv1qgVcokPwkathDueDvIlakURgEgkLzwcmEX4pi8R0g6neAIzsoAKV5ute9ZIFHkyjZb7AZF-m-VPo15W_QQAAP__a2R-1A), standing 6-foot-7 with 24-inch biceps, urging fans to train, take their vitamins, and say their prayers. As the charismatic, shirt-ripping Hulk Hogan, he made wrestling mainstream and became the biggest box-office draw in the sport's history. He also found success in entertainment, starring in a string of movies and TV shows, including _Rocky III_ as Thunderlips, opposite Sylvester Stallone. [See his life in photos here](http://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLFyhCAURb9GO3aeDwS3oEhjt2lTOigPIUFxgKyzf59xfyH1mblzz_l6TA8TYtjXT7ORri5NO50lUq2UJ582ilTKTqWkbCk7UyqVWiYE7Bkohv1kTYivSbRWOyIk3pLuVM8FH6AbWq9hHpwciKRTXBLndjBOIOFCHVccZRv0tQYK-w5A9uqG810tOAMZiQ7M3AggG2rKt-8U9urJxVd6Ur4taWuj9rUepeEfDY4Njua4BC7U4Hj4VBNbTYyUXw2O_jf-MJ9Ws7M3KuzMVOrlz86TGFBHxklrlmEe-DzzrhPqzoVQHBbooc3aHmeIMRSpGgHrZkJ836j_avfU-BcAAP__a6iDKA). Tributes to Bollea [poured in from wrestlers](http://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkb3OnDAQAJ8GukXG_H1XUKShu7Qp0YLX2Il_kHfvEG8fXYq8wNePRhrNr-f6RB98On5ipFlsXhNdHEiEyupypEDMiZhzMVQsshALr1rpAdQEelgN-nCvfW1mS6Spq2lup6Hruy_VftVu3vZ2bIetHbaHUhZ1Zweyj62ddkWGaK_9_LGpSQ-tUuMwNXp7TLveFOGorcKt6hUZL7k0v7NP4siGO7-pNHuOdZidyMlV96PSS6UXPnMRbm50OX-ASi9XIZZPY6UXLOL3QJVezkLsDSUBkxMGA1Je8YS3TztB3CO6nACTgesiYMHCcOINUvz2EgLJ8N8LgQ5KBtwr_AGXD0xwEYTMAghHIRSwxX8IyQZvaMe-7_SoHo2TGOoym_PyIXgep6pXR0Qf_rXJt4a8Z_03AAD__85fpdI) and politicians, with Ric Flair praising their friendship and President Trump calling him "strong, tough, smart, but with the biggest heart."

| | | While far too many people, companies, and organizations have cowered and self-censored in the face of Trump's threats, South Park wasn't afraid to hit Trump HARD (and appropriately) in its season [premiere](https://default.salsalabs.org/T37afdd17-b268-48ff-8ff9-4f1ac1e81593/368d17ff-e836-4168-8049-c5f0900fbbf9) episode. **Its[final scene](https://default.salsalabs.org/Tbfb56c1e-195f-4f5e-862c-1b6c98d6da0b/368d17ff-e836-4168-8049-c5f0900fbbf9) \-- an AI-assisted Trump ad -- may have been one of the most jaw-dropping (and hilarious) moments ever on TV (warning: NSFW). ** And South Park also wasn't afraid to go after Paramount, with which it has a $1.5 billion deal, for its capitulation to Trump a few weeks earlier. Now, we get that South Park's humor isn't for everyone (personally, we love it), but they have consistently produced some of the best social and political satire on TV. And this is exactly what we need to help break through the Trump cult's bubble, when logic and reason alone won't work. So hats off to Trey Parker and Matt Stone (the show's creators), and big thanks to everyone involved. [**_Please join us in saying it: "Thank you, South Park!"_**](https://default.salsalabs.org/T4d4e6d61-dc9c-41d8-be40-a82a6db215f4/368d17ff-e836-4168-8049-c5f0900fbbf9)

name: GOP Presidential
subject: Why We Should Study War
body:
Tech is moving fast. Don’t get left behind. Get your early copy of the Stanford Emerging Tech Review now.

# The Stanford Emerging Tech Review 2025
| | | [](http://e.goppresidential.com/rd/9z2z6aopvu9vuir311i2n4d2p4euhb4rkrsm8kbkj7g_rp22sh2s8i6epb6c5hm8p74cjh2bs)
---
| | Dear Friend,

Wars begin. Freedoms fade. Hard-won peace unravels.

The question is why.

One answer: we've stopped studying military history. And when that knowledge fades, so does our ability to understand today's conflicts--or anticipate tomorrow's.
---
|
[](http://e.goppresidential.com/rd/9z2zc7f40ml59e5b1b8kjcmr03gnbbj5hn5jpj660qg_rp22sh2s8i6epb6c5hm8p74cjh2bs)
---
| | Victor Davis Hanson believes this is no small matter.

In a new ebook from the Hoover Institution, _Why We Should Study War_ , Hanson examines what military history reveals about human nature, conflict, and the cost of preserving peace. His analysis draws on historical case studies and connects them to the challenges facing the world today.

Without knowledge of military history, we risk:
* Repeating past mistakes
* Making uninformed decisions about current and future conflicts
* Undervaluing the sacrifices made for our freedoms

I'd like to share this ebook with you--which includes Hanson's core arguments for studying war along with his answers to key questions about deterrence, WWII, and essential military history reading.

Inside, you'll discover:
* How studying war is, in essence, an attempt to prevent it
* Why human nature and the patterns of conflict remain constant across time
* What battles from Shiloh to Verdun to Okinawa teach us about sacrifice
* How military history provides moral education about the cost of freedom
Why the United States--"born through war, reunited by war, and saved from destruction by war"--must never forget this knowledge
* Understanding the past is essential so we can engage more seriously with the present.

I hope this material deepens your appreciation for military history--and informs how you think about peace, conflict, and public responsibility.

You can request your free copy using the link below:
[https://resources.hoover.org/why-we-should-study-war](http://e.goppresidential.com/rd/9z2zcujina9tlqnc2stkbd6ntf0m6t70sj90ma2k3l0_rp22sh2s8i6epb6c5hm8p74cjh2bs) Greg

Greg Stamps | Online Development
Hoover Institution | Stanford University
With its eminent scholars and world-renowned Library and Archives, the Hoover Institution is a non-partisan, data-driven policy research organization that seeks to improve the human condition by advancing ideas that promote economic prosperity, national security, and democratic governance. Over more than one hundred years, Hoover's work has directly led to policies that have produced greater freedom, democracy, and opportunity in the United States and around the world.

Hoover Institution, 434 Galvez Mall, Stanford University, Stanford, CA 94305 USA

Peter, **“President Trump sees the writing on the wall, and the American people are very unhappy with what's going on right now,”** says Marina Jenkins, Executive Director of the NDRC, in response to the Trump-backed scheme to sway the midterm elections. **“We're looking ahead to what could be a real wave for Democrats, and they're trying to stop that from happening by securing their power before we even get to the elections.”** She’s right, Peter. Donald Trump has asked Texas conservatives to draw a map that would give the GOP _five more_ congressional seats — a brazen attempt to silence the voices of Texas voters who are rightfully angry about Republicans’ extreme MAGA agenda. They know they can’t win fairly, so they’re pushing to hold on to power by gerrymandering. When Republican extremists, let alone the President of the United States, try to gerrymander maps, we have to be prepared to fight back. **That’s why the NDRC is building up our[emergency response efforts](https://click.everyaction.com/k/112090566/559406821/1768578618?refcode=don_ndrc_tier1_email_TXSpecialSession_email_20250725-NDRC-Tier1-TXSpecialSession_&utm_source=email&utm_medium=email&utm_term=don&utm_content=20250725-NDRC-Tier1-TXSpecialSession_&utm_campaign=TXSpecialSession&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9FQS9FQTAxMy8xLzg5Mjk0IiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogImJhNDM5OTIwLTU3NjktZjAxMS04ZGM5LTYwNDViZGE5ZDk2YiIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=VRJ18wZhJQIxdXJrRwiT6bKxUXa_bZiZFRMWYqNKQFo=), to plan for rapid response and mobilization against late-breaking gerrymanders and attacks on free and fair elections.** [**Will you donate to fuel the NDRC’s emergency response efforts and help us be prepared to defend our democracy in Texas and beyond?**](https://click.everyaction.com/k/112090567/559406831/1768578618?refcode=don_ndrc_tier1_email_TXSpecialSession_email_20250725-NDRC-Tier1-TXSpecialSession_&utm_source=email&utm_medium=email&utm_term=don&utm_content=20250725-NDRC-Tier1-TXSpecialSession_&utm_campaign=TXSpecialSession&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9FQS9FQTAxMy8xLzg5Mjk0IiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogImJhNDM5OTIwLTU3NjktZjAxMS04ZGM5LTYwNDViZGE5ZDk2YiIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=VRJ18wZhJQIxdXJrRwiT6bKxUXa_bZiZFRMWYqNKQFo=) [**And if you make it a monthly gift and become a monthly donor to the NDRC, you’ll be automatically entered for a chance to receive a call from our Chair, Attorney General Eric H. The census data also showed that 95% of the state’s population growth came from communities of color. Mary Miller, and Illinois Freedom Caucus Chairman, State Rep. Chris Miller are celebrating their 45th anniversary this week! President Trump had a few words to share as well! Click the image below to watch. | GEORGIA The Swamp is tired of House Freedom Caucus member Congressman Andrew Clyde's conservative record. Check it out: | WYOMING Thanks to the Wyoming Freedom Caucus , the state legislature earlier this year passed a bill that would require that only Wyoming citizens can vote in Wyoming elections. After the bill became law, Marc Elias and the Crazy Left immediately filed a lawsuit. This was a naked attempt to thwart the law and proves Democrats want illegal aliens voting in our elections. But the good news is that a judge struck down the lawsuit earlier this week. The cherry on top of this ruling is that the judge is an Obama-appointee. The Crazy Left can't even convince a liberal judge that this isn't common sense policy! | SOUTH CAROLINA The South Carolina Freedom Caucus has been very vocal about fixing their state's roads and bridges, which are some of the worst in the nation. They are on record, multiple times, urging their colleagues to give up the pork projects and divert the money to real infrastructure repairs. Sadly, they were ignored. It’s outrageous. The worst part? I can bet my mortgage Ashley Moody won’t lift a finger.
[https://d15k2d11r6t6rl.cloudfront.net/public/users/Integrators/04eaa6b2-88f4-43b4-b978-7bb0708f5838/745167472B47686463346337324A2B45635331365A46445A3966303771762B4D5167754770374657435A364251692F42736669372F30664555496B6642443578/editor_images/Screenshot%202025-07-24%20at%203.42.26%E2%80%AFPM.png]
We’re living through record heatwaves, higher utility bills, and flooding in places where people raised their families for generations.
Even if you don’t understand the effects of climate change, your insurance company does.
They’ve jacked up premiums, pulled out of Florida entirely, and left working families footing the bill. That’s not hypothetical. It’s what’s happening right now.
And the response from Trump’s EPA? Give polluters a pass.
I’m running for Senate to fight this exact kind of corruption, the kind where corporate power matters more than clean air, and political headlines matter more than people’s lives.

Peter, discrimination is now legal in at least one American state.

A 35-year-old woman in Tennessee was **denied prenatal care** by her physician because she was “unwed.” According to the _Nashville Banner_ , a physician turned her away because they “didn't feel comfortable treating her” and cited “differing values.”

Although this type of discrimination is illegal across most of America, Tennessee recently passed the Medical Ethics Defense Act. This law grants medical professionals the right to deny healthcare to patients based on their religious, moral, or ethical beliefs. There are no protections for people in rural areas with limited options for healthcare, there are no requirements to refer patients elsewhere, and there’s no legal recourse.

**83% of the lawmakers in Tennessee are _male_.**

We are horrified by this story. We will not sit back as male politicians pass laws that limit women’s bodily autonomy, healthcare, and safety.

[**We cannot accept this reality for our fellow women. We’re working to elect PRO-WOMEN women – especially in red states like Tennessee. This is the first reported case of a woman being denied prenatal care for being unmarried in the state of Tennessee – but it will likely continue to happen more frequently.

The states with the _least amount of women_ in state government almost all have abortion bans and other laws that limit women’s access to healthcare. Tennessee is one of those states. While 3.5 million women live in Tennessee, _women make up only 17% of the state’s government._

The legislator who sponsored this bill, Representative Bryan Terry, said he believed the law would help Tennessee recruit and retain physicians (???!!). In reality, the state has actually seen a _decline_ in OB-GYNs across the state since Tennessee’s total abortion ban went into effect. Tennessee has the highest maternal mortality rate in the country and ranks among the worst for infant mortality.

Derek,

We don’t have to wait until 2026 or 2028 to fight for the soul of our democracy – the fight is happening _right now_ in Pennsylvania.
This November, we will vote in critical races for our state Supreme Court. These justices don’t just interpret the law – they determine how elections are run, whether reproductive rights are protected, and whether extremist efforts to suppress votes are stopped in their tracks.
These are retention races: Voters will be asked “Yes” or “No” on returning sitting justices to the bench. These three were elected in 2015, their terms expire at the end of this year, and all are **highly recommended** by the Pennsylvania Bar Association. Please support the entire Democratic ticket this November, but I’m asking you today to make a plan now to vote “Yes” for:

**Justice Christine Donohue**
**Justice Kevin M. Dougherty**
**Justice David Wecht**
Their seats are critical to maintaining the current **5–2 Democratic majority**. Put simply: If at least two of the justices aren’t retained, Republicans could flip the court for the first time in a decade. They are trying, pouring money into Pennsylvania (and Wisconsin, which is in a similar situation).
The stakes couldn’t be higher. This court has final say on electoral disputes – including in 2028 and beyond. Cases pending before the court right now cover mail-in ballots, use of Medicaid, and women’s reproductive health. Do we want these decisions in the hands of Republicans? No, definitely not the MAGA Republicans who have taken over their party. We’re seeing harmful consequences of that in Washington, D.C.
Pennsylvania isn’t just a battleground – it’s a blueprint. If we show up, organize, and win here, we send a message across the country: Democrats are not backing down.

Your donation will help fund voter outreach, protect ballot access, and ensure that every voice is heard. This fight matters – not just for Pennsylvanians but for our country’s future.

Today is **World IVF Day.** On July 25, 1978, Louise Brown became the first baby born through in vitro fertilization (IVF), a groundbreaking milestone in reproductive medicine. Since then, IVF has helped millions of people around the world build their families. Today, we honor the hope and progress IVF has made possible—while staying vigilant against the threats it faces.

In 2023 alone, IVF led to over 95,000 births in the U.S.—about 2.6% of all births. Despite its widespread use, IVF is still often misunderstood and remains out of reach for many. Our new [**fact sheet**](https://click.everyaction.com/k/112102634/559435606/-970346935?sourceid=1150817&utm_campaign=26emgfl-0701aax-on&utm_medium=ea&utm_source=email&utm_content=frontlines&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9DRlJSL0NGUlIvMS85NTk4MiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIyMjRmMzFjZi01ZjY5LWYwMTEtOGRjOS02MDQ1YmRhOWQ5NmIiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=Tc1MPI_R3xAHoRbo9baVliGfij-vyB4sfRfkTZ5CgFk=&emci=3efa95c9-0368-f011-8dc9-6045bda9d96b&emdi=224f31cf-5f69-f011-8dc9-6045bda9d96b&ceid=954237) breaks down how IVF works, who relies on it, the biggest barriers to access, and the policies needed to ensure everyone can access this essential care.

In 2013, Josephine Majani arrived at Bungoma District Hospital in Kenya in labor, expecting care and compassion. Instead, she was neglected, abused, and forced to give birth on the hospital floor alone and in agony. Her harrowing experience, captured on video, sparked national outrage and ignited a historic legal battle brought by the Center for Reproductive Rights for accountability, justice, and dignity in Kenya's public maternal health system.

A new seven-minute documentary, _Justice for Josephine_ , tells the story of her fight for justice—and the legal victory that affirmed respectful maternity care as a constitutional right in Kenya. In 2024, the Kenya Court of Appeal upheld the ruling, reinforcing the government's obligation to protect the rights and dignity of all women.

The House Judiciary Committee recently passed a bill to repeal the Freedom of Access to Clinic Entrances Act (FACE Act)—a 30-year-old law prohibiting violence against patients, reproductive health care workers, and medical facilities. The bill now heads to the full House floor for a vote.

**Renee Chelian, longtime Center client and founder and CEO of Northland Family Planning Centers in Michigan, submitted testimony for the House Judiciary Committee, describing her experiences with clinic violence and the importance of the FACE Act.**

clean_body: July Front Lines newsletter | | ---|--- | | | | | At the Center for Reproductive Rights, we’re fighting to protect and advance reproductive freedom worldwide. From confronting restrictive abortion policies to championing equity on the global stage, we are dedicated to creating a future where everyone has access to the health care they deserve. Here's a snapshot of our most recent efforts: | Global | | Photo Credit: ©SolStock / iStock | Today is World IVF Day. On July 25, 1978, Louise Brown became the first baby born through in vitro fertilization (IVF), a groundbreaking milestone in reproductive medicine. Since then, IVF has helped millions of people around the world build their families. Today, we honor the hope and progress IVF has made possible—while staying vigilant against the threats it faces. In 2023 alone, IVF led to over 95,000 births in the U.S.—about 2.6% of all births. Despite its widespread use, IVF is still often misunderstood and remains out of reach for many. Our new breaks down how IVF works, who relies on it, the biggest barriers to access, and the policies needed to ensure everyone can access this essential care. | | Africa | | | In 2013, Josephine Majani arrived at Bungoma District Hospital in Kenya in labor, expecting care and compassion. Instead, she was neglected, abused, and forced to give birth on the hospital floor alone and in agony. Her harrowing experience, captured on video, sparked national outrage and ignited a historic legal battle brought by the Center for Reproductive Rights for accountability, justice, and dignity in Kenya's public maternal health system. A new seven-minute documentary, Justice for Josephine , tells the story of her fight for justice—and the legal victory that affirmed respectful maternity care as a constitutional right in Kenya. In 2024, the Kenya Court of Appeal upheld the ruling, reinforcing the government's obligation to protect the rights and dignity of all women. | | United States | | | The House Judiciary Committee recently passed a bill to repeal the Freedom of Access to Clinic Entrances Act (FACE Act)—a 30-year-old law prohibiting violence against patients, reproductive health care workers, and medical facilities. The bill now heads to the full House floor for a vote. Renee Chelian, longtime Center client and founder and CEO of Northland Family Planning Centers in Michigan, submitted testimony for the House Judiciary Committee, describing her experiences with clinic violence and the importance of the FACE Act. Repealing the FACE Act would encourage even more attacks and violence against abortion patients and providers. President Donald Trump visited the Federal Reserve Wednesday, **[confronting Fed Chairman Jerome Powell](https://substack.com/redirect/d4de8ba4-00e7-4f3a-9b20-aab7359041a9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** for spending over $3 billion tax dollars for lavish new renovations at the bank's headquarters.
[Click To Watch Video](https://substack.com/redirect/d4de8ba4-00e7-4f3a-9b20-aab7359041a9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
[](https://substack.com/redirect/d4de8ba4-00e7-4f3a-9b20-aab7359041a9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
"It went up a little bit, or a lot. So the $2.7 billion is now $3.1," Trump asserted, speaking to press about the renovation costs with Powell right next to him shaking his head in protest.
"I'm not aware of that," Powell told Trump. "I haven't heard that from anyone at the Fed."
Trump slowly reached into his pocket and pulled out a piece of paper with the building costs to support his claim. "It just came out..."
* **President Trump claimed there was "no tension" between him and Powell** during their meeting, despite visible awkwardness on camera and Trump's recent public attacks on Powell over interest rates.

If you would like to unsubscribe, visit this | | | | | Dear Friend, Your participation in Hillsdale College's National Survey on the United States Supreme Court is requested. Your response will only take a few minutes, but the subject is crucial to the future of liberty and the separation of powers in America. The American Founders thought that the proper role of the Supreme Court is to apply the Constitution. But progressives see the Court differently. They want activist judges to legislate from the bench. Do you agree that the role of the Supreme Court is to apply the Constitution as it is written and NOT to make laws or advance a particular policy agenda? Even worse, progressives dismayed by recent Supreme Court decisions want to "pack" the bench with additional justices to advance a preferred policy agenda. As Sen. Elizabeth Warren (D-Mass.) put it in a Boston Globe op-ed: "To restore balance and integrity to a broken institution, Congress must expand the Supreme Court by four or more seats." What is your opinion about the Supreme Court's role in our constitutional republic? Please share your thoughts with me using the College's National Survey on the United States Supreme Court right away. Your response will help Hillsdale form effective strategies to educate millions of Americans about the importance of the Constitution to liberty--including the proper role of an independent judiciary that applies the Constitution instead of legislating from the bench. You can easily complete your National Survey on the United States Supreme Court using this secure link: And after you give your views, I hope you will consider supporting Hillsdale College with a tax-deductible gift. The failure of too many of America's schools to provide young people with a proper education in American history and government makes it easier for progressives to undermine the separation of powers at the heart of limited government. I'm sure you agree that too many Americans do not understand the role of an independent judiciary in preserving our constitutional order. That's why Hillsdale College has expanded its educational outreach efforts on behalf of liberty nationwide, directly reaching and teaching millions of Americans in all 50 states--including yours! These efforts counter the influence of anti-American ideology being taught in classrooms all across America. Your support will help us to expand our educational outreach, including: Teaching millions of citizens nationwide through free online courses, such as "Constitution 101: The Meaning and History of the Constitution" and "The U.S. Supreme Court." Reaching over six million households and businesses nationwide with Imprimis , Hillsdale's free digest of liberty Sending millions of pocket-size copies of America's founding documents to citizens, teachers, and students in K-12 schools across America. Restoring excellence to K-12 education by launching and providing ongoing guidance to over 70 classical K-12 charter schools nationwide that offer a strong American history and civics curriculum. We undertake our educational outreach efforts on behalf of liberty --as we do all of our work--without accepting a penny of government funding, not even indirectly in the form of federal or state student grants or loans. That means all of our work--including reaching and teaching millions about America's great heritage of liberty--depends entirely on the support of Americans like you, who understand the importance of education to liberty. Please share your thoughts with Hillsdale using the College's National Survey on the United States Supreme Court right away--the link is below. Derek, In just a few days, we’ll reach our next end-of-month fundraising deadline. We’re going to ask you to [**make your first contribution of 2025 to help us reach our goal before that deadline**](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em-dnc-july-2025?amount=3&refcode=em_20250725_4060_fr&refcode2=4060_22930333_9xWxRu&akid=4060%2E22930333%2E9xWxRu) in just a minute, but first, we want to tell you what we’ve been able to accomplish this month with the help of grassroots supporters _just like you_. subject: July Wins from Team Healey-Driscoll
disclaimer_text: Paid for by the Massachusetts Democratic State Committee
body:
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/NGP/NGP31/1/93809/images/Logo.png]
Dear Peter;
July was another exciting month for Team Healey-Driscoll, including huge wins for Massachusetts families, renters, and students. Here are just some of the impactful accomplishments from July that the Gov and Lt. Gov are excited to celebrate:
* As part of her continued focus on lowering costs for residents, on July 21 Governor Healey announced that the Division of Insurance has negotiated down proposed rate increases from six health insurers, saving Massachusetts residents and businesses a projected $4.5 million in health care premiums for 2026.
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/NGP/NGP31/1/93809/images/54663121186_f3f9d6e2f8_c.jpg]
* On July 17, Governor Healey signed an executive order [https://www.mass.gov/executive-orders/no-643-establishing-the-governors-anti-hunger-task-force] establishing an Anti-Hunger Task Force that will work to prevent Massachusetts families from going hungry as President Trump cuts food assistance for children, seniors, veterans and people with disabilities.
* On July 16, the Healey-Driscoll Administration announced the launch of the Live Theater Tax Credit Pilot Program to support new and growing live theatrical production throughout Massachusetts.
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/NGP/NGP31/1/93809/images/54657645776_7b2dae96db_c.jpg]
* On July 15, Governor Healey proclaimed July 15th as WNBA Day in Boston in Massachusetts and called for a WNBA team in Boston.
* On July 15, Lieutenant Governor Driscoll testified in support of the Mass Ready Act, a $3 billion investment to streamline permitting for housing, strengthen infrastructure, protect clean water and prepare for extreme weather.
* On July 10, CNBC named Massachusetts as the Most Improved State for Business [https://www.cnbc.com/2025/07/10/massachusetts-most-improved-state-for-business-america.html] , jumping 18 spots from the previous year and ranking higher than any other New England state.
* On July 10, data released by the state's Department of Higher Ed showed that MassReconnect, Governor Healey’s cost-free community college program for students ages 25 and older, continued drawing adult learners to Massachusetts’ community colleges in its second year. According to the new data, community college enrollment of new students ages 25+ without a prior college degree grew by 39.6 percent between the fall 2023 and 2024 semesters.
* On July 9, Governor Healey called for a bell-to-bell cellphone ban in public schools with options for parents to contact their children during the school day. The Governor says a ban will support parents and teachers, protect the mental health of young people, and help our students learn and grow.
* On July 4, Governor Healey signed the Fiscal Year 2026 (FY26) state budget [https://www.mass.gov/news/governor-healey-signs-609-billion-fiscal-year-2026-budget] , a $60.9 billion plan to make Massachusetts more affordable, improve transportation, invest in the state's world-class education system, and grow the economy.
* On July 2, Governor Healey announced that the Fiscal Year 2026 budget would include her proposal to eliminate renter-paid broker’s fees. In January, Governor Healey filed an outside section in her FY26 budget proposal that would require the fee to be paid by whoever hires the broker, which is usually the landlord.
We're so grateful for Team Healey-Driscoll and their work on behalf of our Commonwealth!
Onward,
MassDems

name: Lindsey Graham
subject: My story, Fellow American
body:
I learned some tough lessons early on. |
---
I want to share something from the heart with you, Fellow American.

**_My story._**
It isn't one of glitz and glamour -- it's about hard work, loss, and fighting for what's right. I'm reaching out to tell you why I'm in this fight for our future, and why I need you with me.

Neither of my parents finished high school. But they were hardworking and determined that their children would surpass their achievements.

Most of my growing up happened on the main street of a small textile mill town. My parents had a business establishment -- a combination beer joint, restaurant, liquor store, and pool hall -- known as the Sanitary Cafe right on Main Street in Central, SC. We all lived in the back of the bar where we worked late into the evening, especially my mom, before heading off to bed in the backroom.

[](http://links.justandfreegop.com/u/click?_t=8ca5ef3d31cc43bcb1fbe6968d953911&_m=2d8773d930cf46c18c18080eee5016f8&_e=G8-N_wxIEAl1BbFcG7600xeARtnjj60dC-aHc6M4-vd8g6hc6AkMWZF7QaYLPatTaXXnSfSsisV2RaLq4wr4f1-ejCk62SejJTKXr2mEgQevprdw-1oW4T62facPlzqQvCzqot6y7AyT87Dj5Zx4lBwUeQxw_UI4r8llDStCAUHktp1fHbJZMnZh3OyUaOdBn9SggcvMhINP1SV9LVE0QRwFrDVgSCi5bz6mqpz9U26xyEvfGMnZ5JKPzHQmYijMrfCXAIOaotCcAjUSxZlhjXV5RP5pt2bH9rNTPCVgiLOsa6oOplpNANQ8PuB7vlEW8fN09S6HbNiOgAaP-wQDoJTW1FznsnLU8RE_QxHnOKG3YJZs7UH9IzpTADfXTNmo2z_y6rnDi-AFaO7XHxpB2qJbUX-WcWsLWH8Cg7TEw5tmRZg1-n-wvpIhtTOe96p6mfBFFfu-CZ3-xS0AMS7Ryf7YSEmNl7XSiGd-NWAt2aM8BaS4_0GwGCBudnMy8EE1WmXF-0649yexcc-l4nQFb5xbOpFyvokL7MY6VLiZPTfjBe58R9M2UbUri3JHw2m9-OGMm6h21Ti3qdwC10wDWSD7Yo35VSAkVFgkNbFLCc1E6EOBDvQSTweusMg7eWMXn8fUIpG7Bs0bOMt0ji2mAq2VyTIeA6cWNZ2FTZj2es3qFwPSYGrN9zZQqHY7REFK) I had no silver spoon in my mouth but I never felt I was missing out on something because I didn't live in a house like my friends did. I had a great life, and it was a great way to grow up.

I was the first in my family to attend college, but then life hit me hard. While I was in school, I lost my mom and dad within two years of each other. And just like that, I stepped up to help raise my 13-year-old sister, Darline, while coming back home on the weekends to help at our family business.

[](http://links.justandfreegop.com/u/click?_t=8ca5ef3d31cc43bcb1fbe6968d953911&_m=2d8773d930cf46c18c18080eee5016f8&_e=G8-N_wxIEAl1BbFcG7600xeARtnjj60dC-aHc6M4-vd8g6hc6AkMWZF7QaYLPatTaXXnSfSsisV2RaLq4wr4f1-ejCk62SejJTKXr2mEgQevprdw-1oW4T62facPlzqQvCzqot6y7AyT87Dj5Zx4lBwUeQxw_UI4r8llDStCAUHktp1fHbJZMnZh3OyUaOdBn9SggcvMhINP1SV9LVE0QRwFrDVgSCi5bz6mqpz9U27DvO1xhgc6CwvZTf8i1iIBApt2o1YEcWzfhe8d-4x54hXRUFocYZXUGDupLuKoqyZdSOSxkN50C3maDzyBR5qd9qjbf8Nz01pevg87-uNuHLS7DJJrbLFcTPJOG8WRUXyWXuk_MFuq0vkik5PgKcEl42CjTB3xqirwn0vnuA08j29Yo0W3SK7SHRVhQwDCJDNDSd4oiOFnpS1HjDDo30cKHRMBVD3l_Ic0m731hkjohnERFco0SOWBBpppUP1vhxHgiQMDTWrbvd-Qs-OYqwPzXkBAZLIxWQsRQsT2Tcej28DqO-AGJXN7j5d_do0XfJBcTfixrRwNwRd_Z8z9E5ZjGjEFIS1DA99PlaP0ZGmA2FsLUaODyprnBEwj5VgLRwHWJTYiwkiRA6uvRn-Qj-5B5TyOBPp66fTAB1nW8GR20y5FthV5QT7dLAy0v0KjpNZYNeimPi03kC2At0A_Nzqe) **Fellow American, I learned some tough lessons early on.**

After law school, I joined the U.S. Air Force as a Judge Advocate General, serving as a military prosecutor and defense attorney. Even after the people of South Carolina sent me to the United States Senate, I continued my service in the Air Force Reserves. I performed several short deployments in war zones like Afghanistan and Iraq, standing shoulder to shoulder with our brave men and women in uniform.

My story isn't all that different from yours or most people across this great country. I didn't have anything handed to me. I worked hard, grew up quickly, and took on big responsibilities.

**But what shaped me most was listening to the hard -working South Carolinians who'd come by our family business, sharing their hopes and struggles, or hearing the perspectives of my brave colleagues in the military.** _Whether I agreed with them or not, those conversations built my understanding of what Americans need and deserve._

Now, Fellow American, we all know our nation's in a tough spot -- we're divided, but there are some things we should agree on, plain and simple.

**🇺🇸 We need a country where you can raise your family without fear, where the streets are safe.**
**🇺🇸 We need a country where the American Dream isn't just a slogan.**
_It's alive, and every hard -working American has a real shot at it, no matter where they start._
**[That's what I'm fighting for every single day, Fellow American.](http://links.justandfreegop.com/u/click?_t=8ca5ef3d31cc43bcb1fbe6968d953911&_m=2d8773d930cf46c18c18080eee5016f8&_e=G8-N_wxIEAl1BbFcG7600xeARtnjj60dC-aHc6M4-vd8g6hc6AkMWZF7QaYLPatTaXXnSfSsisV2RaLq4wr4f1-ejCk62SejJTKXr2mEgQevprdw-1oW4T62facPlzqQvCzqot6y7AyT87Dj5Zx4lBwUeQxw_UI4r8llDStCAUHktp1fHbJZMnZh3OyUaOdBn9SggcvMhINP1SV9LVE0QRwFrDVgSCi5bz6mqpz9U278XbVfG2L7A_3LgL1twy6fEr7fN78GtTVMYuRbraOcqyJiVgjeTnq3G_i8fjcrgbxV-s3QIFm-Z21Mq_asjRB2FLUpe3rvmA08HNwbtO279BkGi6w88qjdcOpAz_U3rh0XtjAvb2if3AwNY7p1S3g0N7vnZst58VAjlxdO7Ajdhi8OCzIvHSeSeF883OpAeGikNfa7LKDJ9b9tqLURX9dOxuev2d1rfikQoqrF2vN7EX95p9kcsDaSPNZJM5xN7IwpZh-deKbfnMw6EeaBN25hDVLEk99WnNrPxwLbxEJ070e58wIAwJebBWjCPrMmEvmNdyunX0TFrUzdrAjZqo_9g0yoEHmmv79VQZ_Oj2wMTWKJJJKb4rOf5zCss5lauji3PZwuoJ42snBeoa3wDbfnrTYspMoprwkB8bwqifb0fJwG9LTNpQLa_UqbSjlATag7IlSUlec0ncd95dDqIq-S)**

Sadly, there are folks in Washington, across the aisle, who don't see it that way. They're fine with open borders, allowing violent crime spill into our neighborhoods. They're okay with slapping higher taxes on hard-working folks like you, piling more burdens on your family. That isn't right, and I won't stand for it.

So I'm coming to you with a simple ask, Fellow American. If you've got a few dollars to spare, **[would you consider joining Team Graham to support my campaign?](http://links.justandfreegop.com/u/click?_t=8ca5ef3d31cc43bcb1fbe6968d953911&_m=2d8773d930cf46c18c18080eee5016f8&_e=G8-N_wxIEAl1BbFcG7600xeARtnjj60dC-aHc6M4-vd8g6hc6AkMWZF7QaYLPatTaXXnSfSsisV2RaLq4wr4f1-ejCk62SejJTKXr2mEgQevprdw-1oW4T62facPlzqQvCzqot6y7AyT87Dj5Zx4lBwUeQxw_UI4r8llDStCAUHktp1fHbJZMnZh3OyUaOdBn9SggcvMhINP1SV9LVE0QRwFrDVgSCi5bz6mqpz9U247GI2FN-ifpMxAmzit2hiqUSbS9iWgeidoqibgsRSMf8EQnWg_pArEdZbeh-XIxHp32qNioEsYTyo2aQ5MfCU1JCeBwE8C-oXKIsCVmyKQf-ReQuLiAboiiJoGTSi3SOgb2lKd_T9xSmjles7nVhAptb_VyCyfrC0dPcaow6ZpeYeW7AMphUGE6-rbwd97W9GZaSzOPPgY0nJnNG2j93DDAZaxWFfMqabqhX8u79QBguY8_9aDesDRf1AK0YEOGVQH2iejFaKEKLfXhwEfujsMMpVoZs9oeWMmfoFSZKLdmaEdPiCfkJnkWI8X8z_q4LbuUoMASiGvP_zfjhq06ZPCPnhlLuyyy2Olpw9XZb6EanqHa8Xh03_NPbcsL2tyf7RypEfrZ9r0QPttUBtCNA7gen03YYmyr2zO6Kio2wm9sdH69GfrCd2ccZn5g6s0lCIdoLWFkjBxhlRuOMHvBfUf)**

| [**JOIN TEAM GRAHAM >>**](http://links.justandfreegop.com/u/click?_t=8ca5ef3d31cc43bcb1fbe6968d953911&_m=2d8773d930cf46c18c18080eee5016f8&_e=G8-N_wxIEAl1BbFcG7600xeARtnjj60dC-aHc6M4-vd8g6hc6AkMWZF7QaYLPatTaXXnSfSsisV2RaLq4wr4f1-ejCk62SejJTKXr2mEgQevprdw-1oW4T62facPlzqQvCzqot6y7AyT87Dj5Zx4lBwUeQxw_UI4r8llDStCAUHktp1fHbJZMnZh3OyUaOdBn9SggcvMhINP1SV9LVE0QRwFrDVgSCi5bz6mqpz9U27O5X5lgR_kwAWIgks4vpneDn3ih7qHK-aUkYR0uZ3yg87ZpQGrZP3szAMGiUIFE60vg13OHI80I4FvGR3lRifDR8kb12VOxxAnbFIA46PzX90gDiLME5001SO2V1y55oS5ifELq-49sO4P69MQClnSTVG6N34GF0EL9xnxwqqh8myaWGdOp_BzkWBODTJ2b6nk5QYKk2-3SgUBIVU_r-zO1A9u7ohT_bCJyJn0NUFQulDgQ0SE31JNh18zYWQO8DH_oVibNG1bCHA6uJDxKcH3efeR62HKsdSx2QVMiMIfbWMpOTegNo2JkHlILKjuj3RtIeulPEDGhonI6oDm4dACB52TrRXooIX9fx-hp_gYp3LdAQrf15Lj2HnsziLQIsr9a_JZnbMluQxKQh24ZAiRH9xnMgrnXGRvGMmwOJi41BmJMadjhREf8ONcPa_sKvpXITczqVpMdUB9fYAzhxRo)
---

clean_body: I learned some tough lessons early on. | I want to share something from the heart with you, Fellow American. My story. It isn't one of glitz and glamour -- it's about hard work, loss, and fighting for what's right. I'm reaching out to tell you why I'm in this fight for our future, and why I need you with me. Neither of my parents finished high school. But they were hardworking and determined that their children would surpass their achievements. Most of my growing up happened on the main street of a small textile mill town. My parents had a business establishment -- a combination beer joint, restaurant, liquor store, and pool hall -- known as the Sanitary Cafe right on Main Street in Central, SC. We all lived in the back of the bar where we worked late into the evening, especially my mom, before heading off to bed in the backroom. I had no silver spoon in my mouth but I never felt I was missing out on something because I didn't live in a house like my friends did. I had a great life, and it was a great way to grow up. I was the first in my family to attend college, but then life hit me hard. While I was in school, I lost my mom and dad within two years of each other. And just like that, I stepped up to help raise my 13-year-old sister, Darline, while coming back home on the weekends to help at our family business. Fellow American, I learned some tough lessons early on. After law school, I joined the U.S. Air Force as a Judge Advocate General, serving as a military prosecutor and defense attorney. Even after the people of South Carolina sent me to the United States Senate, I continued my service in the Air Force Reserves. I performed several short deployments in war zones like Afghanistan and Iraq, standing shoulder to shoulder with our brave men and women in uniform. My story isn't all that different from yours or most people across this great country. I didn't have anything handed to me. I worked hard, grew up quickly, and took on big responsibilities. But what shaped me most was listening to the hard -working South Carolinians who'd come by our family business, sharing their hopes and struggles, or hearing the perspectives of my brave colleagues in the military. Whether I agreed with them or not, those conversations built my understanding of what Americans need and deserve. Now, Fellow American, we all know our nation's in a tough spot -- we're divided, but there are some things we should agree on, plain and simple. 🇺🇸 We need a country where you can raise your family without fear, where the streets are safe. 🇺🇸 We need a country where the American Dream isn't just a slogan. It's alive, and every hard -working American has a real shot at it, no matter where they start. Sadly, there are folks in Washington, across the aisle, who don't see it that way. They're fine with open borders, allowing violent crime spill into our neighborhoods. They're okay with slapping higher taxes on hard-working folks like you, piling more burdens on your family. That isn't right, and I won't stand for it. So I'm coming to you with a simple ask, Fellow American. Yesterday, I stood outside a heavily damaged sewage pump station in Hillsborough and gave a press conference.
It was about 91 degrees. Reporters were sweating.
Here's the story.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/91013430-10c9-4520-a755-252c076ed9e8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* * *
I'm suing FEMA.
Why?
Because they illegally cancelled more than $200 million that was headed to North Carolina for water and sewer upgrades.
It was basically a flood preparation fund. Congress created it, funded it, and told FEMA to run it.
Before FEMA pulled the plug, they had approved over 60 projects across our state - mostly moving pump stations and sewer lines to higher ground.
A few examples:
* $22.5m for Salisbury to move a pump station. The city already spent $3m of its own funds getting started.
* $5.9m for Gastonia to move sewer lines out of the floodplain.
* $4m for Mt. Pleasant to improve drainage in the town center, which regularly floods and damages businesses.

And then there's the Hillsborough pump station, where I spoke yesterday. It was set to receive $6m to move to higher ground. Also cancelled by FEMA.
But here's the thing:
Three weeks ago, a tropical storm hit. The nearby river rose 24 feet and submerged the entire station. _Millions of gallons_ of untreated sewage poured into the river.
I spotlighted this pump station because it's a perfect example of why this funding matters - and what happens when it's taken away.
Most people agree that keeping drinking water flowing and sewage contained is a legitimate use of public dollars. I appreciate that Sen. Tillis and Rep. Edwards have also urged FEMA to reverse course.
Heck, President Trump signed this program into law in his first term. He wanted it.
So we're going to court, along with a number of AGs, and I'll report back.
### **Update on frozen education funds**
Speaking of frozen funds that likely violate federal law...
Remember the freeze on $165m of education funding I told you about last week?
Two updates:
First, the Department of Education partially backtracked. It unfroze about $36m, specifically the funding for after-school and summer programs that serve over 10,000 kids in North Carolina.
That's good, but it still leaves roughly $130m unlawfully frozen, so we're going to court to get the rest.
Second, 10 Republican Senators signed a letter urging the Department to reverse course, giving us a strong bipartisan front going forward. That's helpful.
The next step is a request for an emergency hearing to try and get this resolved before the school year starts.
By the way, I visited the Dream Center in Gastonia this week. It's a nonprofit that provides high quality summer and after-school instruction - and receives about half of its funding from one of these programs. I wanted to see their work firsthand, and I was impressed. If more people could see what I saw, it might shift perspectives and lower the temperature a bit.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/56a153c7-26e2-4534-9cd6-9b18a4ee80ce?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
### **Lighthouse success**
The response to our Lighthouse Fund has been incredible.
Over 1,000 of you have chipped in, making this a clear success.
If you haven't joined yet, I hope you'll consider it. The idea is simple: create a low-cost way to stay in touch with voters through a once-a-month digital message - like a steady beam from a lighthouse.
It's a bit of an experiment, but given how many people are cutting the cord and going all-digital, we think it could be a really effective way to reach them.
The best way to support this effort is a small monthly donation, but of course, one-time contributions are also welcome. You can do either **[here](https://substack.com/redirect/6c536730-a4bd-4490-a043-46cc58d5505a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** (ActBlue) or **[here](https://substack.com/redirect/753e027d-3b52-4c06-aee9-dd62b1f2eae0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** (non-ActBlue).
Thanks again.
\- Jeff Jackson

* * *

**P.S. -** One more small request. I know anxiety levels are pretty high for a lot of people right now. I get it. In these emails, I try to replace some of that anxiety with information. People usually feel a little better when they've got a clearer sense of what's happening. ## Colbert OUT: Political attack or common sense?
It's official: [Steven Colbert is out at CBS](https://substack.com/redirect/28ca206d-cc02-4dad-915e-0959c93760ec?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
He's not just fired, CBS is scrapping The Late Show altogether.
Maybe media is finally healing.
But to hear the Left talk, you'd think that Trump personally walked up to the CBS headquarters and demanded Colbert get the boot.
They're crying foul, saying that Colbert was fired because of Trump-- that CBS just folded to pressure from the President.
Remember how Trump received settlements from ABC and CBS for libel and dishonest coverage?
The Left seems to think Colbert is the most recent casualty of those settlements.
Let's put aside the legitimacy of those settlements for a second (spoiler: the networks _were_ in the wrong, that's why they had to pay up).
I have my own brilliant theory about why Colbert was sacked--it's a little complicated but I think it makes sense.
Colbert was a bad host.
The Late Show was a bad show.
CBS is tired of losing money so they're switching things up.
Makes sense to me, but let's break it down. ...

Hi folks, it’s Congressman Robert Garcia, the top Democrat on the House Oversight Committee.
**This week, we fought for transparency and accountability on the Epstein files and won.**
Thanks to our efforts and your support, Republicans agreed to pass a motion to force the Department of Justice to release the Epstein files.
[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/112120973/559468105/789508428?refcode=250725_RG_subpoena&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTIvMS85MTcxOSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIwYzljMzJkOC03MDY5LWYwMTEtOGRjOS02MDQ1YmRhOWQ5NmIiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=T9VsovKa4n_bqsB3-nugaanFpulLr0U2umQvmP9UbhU=)
Let’s be clear: this is a huge win for the American people. The public deserves to know who was complicit in Epstein’s heinous crimes, including people with immense power in our government.
This week's vote was just the first step toward accountability, and we will continue pushing for the truth.

clean_body: See how you’re empowering the next generation of organizers: | | | Peter, Your support makes everything we do possible, especially when it comes to training the next generation of organizers. We asked our members what it means to power their communities, and what kind of future we can achieve if we all stand together. Their responses show that your support isn’t just financial, it’s transformational. | | | Q: What does it mean to power your community? In what ways are you showing up to power your communities at school, at work, and in your family or friend groups? A: “I power up my community by making time for joy and celebration.They sow chaos while we sow love.” “My community is powered by love. That is why I fight every day to ensure all public school students are treated with dignity. Instead of punishing or criminalizing Black, brown, transgender and gender nonconforming, and immigrant youth,we should support youth so they can develop their own power and agency.” “ I am showing up to local board meetings to demand that the police stop collaborating with ICE.I'm getting trained on rapid response for when ICE shows up in my neighborhood or my place of work.” | Q: What kind of future can we build when we all stand together? A: “ When we the people come together, we can fight for a future where everyone feels safe, everyone feels valued and heard.I want my child to grow up in a world that celebrates our differences with love and understanding and empathy.” “I believe a just and liberated future for ALL of us is possible — one where we share joy, celebrate our unique gifts, strive, struggle, and grow in community, honor and listen to each other, make space for restoration and rest, nurture creativity, and practice radical love. Together we can tear down white supremacy in all its forms, build communities, states, and a country where we all belong and have what we need... Everyone, including my immigrant neighbors, are in this vision — because we are already home.” While our communities are threatened, we continue to come together to show that it’s people, not billionaires, who will turn the tide.
