SO YOU'VE PROBABLY HEARD THERE'S A STORM BREWING IN MISSISSIPPI. If you haven't, I hate to be the bearer of bad news, but almost everyone in the state is about to see their property taxes take a huge leap up.
I've had several folks reach out to me over the past few weeks when they found this information out to ask if this substantial increase was coming from some kind of legislation passed by the Mississippi legislature? There has also been some who have voiced their concerns that it is just a ploy by an our local tax assessor and/or county and city officials to rake in millions more in tax dollars.
Surprisingly, let me begin by saying that none of these things are the real reason. It was actually an administrative directive from the Mississippi Department of Revenue (DOR), not a specific statute passed by the Legislature this year, or some kind of sinister master plan by local leaders.
To be honest, this information even caught me by surprise. Thankfully, the county that I live in (Desoto) decided to send out notices to everyone breaking the bad news. I guess they were trying to soften the blow we would all experience when letters started to arrive from our mortgage companies outlining the deficit in our escrow accounts, and the subsequent hike in our monthly note. If you own your house outright, you probably wouldn't even have known until you got your next property tax bill later this fall or early next year.
Here is exactly what happened:
• Under existing Mississippi law (Miss. Code § 27‐35‐1 and related sections), tax assessors are required to appraise real property "at true value" and perform physical inspections at least once every four years.
• In July 2025, the DOR directed all county assessors to update their manuals and increase their valuation index--raising assessed property values to at least 85 % of fair market value (with the goal of reaching 100%).
• That instruction, not a bill, is why you're seeing widespread reassessments and significant increases.
Now this doesn't completely exempt our local leaders, as I will address later in this post (as there is something they can do about it). Most of us in Desoto and surrounding counties have not witnessed big increases in our property taxes over the last 5 years (especially if you live out in the county like I do). I know that our county leadership has tried hard to keep the millage the same for decades, and property valuation and increases to a minimum.
Since Covid, we've witnessed historic property value increases. Supply and demand, along with high inflation and associated building costs are many of the reasons for this increase. Sadly, it doesn't just stop with valuations and prices though, everything associated with homeownership has gone up. I have a moderate sized home (1500 square feet), and just this year had my homeowners insurance premiums increase by 50%! All the excuses from my insurance company, and subsequent ones that I shopped around with after receiving that premium increase, pointed out the increases in home costs, labor, and replacement values associated with home ownership.
So why doesn't the county just ignore the directive from DOR? The fact is that if you live in Mississippi, and you live in the house that you own, you can file for and receive a Homestead exemption which will significantly lower your property taxes. You can also get an additional and substantial Homestead exemption once you reach the age of 65 too. That exemption/discount which is extended to the homeowner, is reimbursed by the state back to the local jurisdictions. It was the state's way of helping out counties and municipalities, along with its homeowners when it came to taxes and home ownership.
Here's the rub, the Department of Revenue has told local jurisdiction that they must get their assessments up to fair value or risk losing that reimbursement. I don't know what or who was the impetus for this sudden threat, but without the reimbursement from the state, Desoto County would find itself tens of millions of dollars to the negative, and the homestead exemptions we enjoy would probably go away all together. I assume your county would be no different if you live elsewhere.
I had one friend ask why the legislature couldn't just change the existing law that DOR is expecting enforcement of. While that is always a possibility, it's not necessarily prudent. Fair value is what everything from our insurance premiums, ad valorem taxes, and other purchase that we make are based. To give a Tax Assessor the freedom to assess whatever price he or she wants to a home (as opposed to it being based on fair value), could create perverse incentives for individuals who have wealth and political influence gaining unfair assessment in places where there are unscrupulous elected leaders.
As of right now, according to the law, you CAN challenge your assessment value if you feel it is too high (which would result in your paying more property taxes than you rightfully should). However, without the measuring stick of "fair value", there would be no grounds to challenge an unfair valuation of your property. It's a catch 22. If you feel your local leaders have under assessed the value of your home, my advice would be to just keep your mouth shut and enjoy the fact your tax burden will be less as a result. Their assessment has no bearing on the actual market value of your home (what you can ask and sell it for). IF YOU FEEL YOUR ASSESEMENT IS TOO HIGH, MANY COUNTIES ARE REQUIRING THAT YOU MUST CHALLENGE IT BY JULY 31, 2025.
In case you are not aware, your property taxes consist of three different taxing entities/recipients: your city if you live in one, your county, and your local school district. NOW HERE IS WHERE THE LOCAL LEADERS BEAR RESPONSIBILITY. Many of them will tell you that they have no choice but to raise the assessment value of your property (true). As a result, this raise will increase the amount of taxes you will now have to pay (also true). Never forget though, that they are the one's who set the millage rate. The millage is a multiplier used to determine how much you have to pay in taxes on your property. It is applied to and based on your assessed valuation. If your local municipality or county raises your assessment value (and as a result your taxes), which ultimately results in increased revenue for that said municipality or county, THEN THEY TOO HAVE RAISED YOUR TAXES (not just DOR). Local leaders have the power to adjust your millage rate down to compensate or offset any increase in revenue that they might otherwise experience from this reassessment.
If your local leaders ran on platforms that they would not raise your taxes, that they would be fiscally conservative and responsible with your tax dollars, and then turn around and tell you that there is nothing that they can do about any increased revenues that they might experience as a result of the reassessment...THEN THEY ARE LYING TO YOU. This fact also applies to your local school district, since they will also be a major beneficiary of any increases in property values assessed to you. They too posses the same ability to raise or lower their millage portion to offset for any actual increases that they realize as a result of this reassessment.
If you know me and my voting record, along with the many fights I have taken up in my 10 years of service to my constituents and our state, then you know I have fought for your pocketbooks and freedoms at every turn. As much as I hate this new increase in valuations and what it potentially mean for both of us, it is not necessarily the fault of either your legislators or local leadership. How much of an increase though that any of us experience, will be determined not just by the Department of Revenue's directive...but also our Supervisors, Mayors, Alderman, and School Boards if their coffers also increase as a result.
Talk to your local leadership, consider enlisting the help of your legislators in doing the same. I have, and as a result I know that our county and some of its municipalities are planning to reduce millage rates to offset the increase and still be in compliance with the law and the DOR directive.

subject: News from First Lady Dawn Moore
body:

| Hello Friends and Fellow Marylanders, This first half of the year has been one of the most powerful and inspiring of my time as your First Lady—from establishing the inaugural Preakness Festival, supporting our military families, meeting the newest graduates of the University of Baltimore, honoring our heritage and commitment to our future, and kicking off the start to summer. I’ve been reminded again and again of what makes Maryland so special—our people. This season has been about lifting others as we lead. As an administration, we've worked to grow our economy, uplift communities that have been historically disenfranchised, support our people during crisis, and partner with the General Assembly to pass legislation to move our state forward. This is the impact we continue to make as we keep our promise to leave no one behind. I can’t wait for what’s ahead and working with all Marylanders to make it happen. Thank you for being on this journey with me. Take Care, **First Lady Dawn Moore** |
* * *
---

### [Maryland First Lady Dawn Moore is Turning the Preakness Stakes into a $400M Celebration of Culture and Community](https://links-1.govdelivery.com/CL0/https:%2F%2Fwww.essence.com%2Flifestyle%2Fmaryland-first-lady-dawn-moore-reimagines-preakness-stakes%2F/1/0100019842662f0a-01c93890-317d-416c-9bbd-45f033f84f84-000000/t1Fkn1txLX0fzwsnlE-_s56XjpuFozI8NQ_gFsOdjiE=415)
The inaugural [Preakness Festival](https://links-1.govdelivery.com/CL0/https:%2F%2Fwww.baltimoresun.com%2F2025%2F05%2F12%2Fdawn-moore-maryland-is-making-preakness-better-than-ever-before-guest-commentary%2F/1/0100019842662f0a-01c93890-317d-416c-9bbd-45f033f84f84-000000/jDF0X4P2EOiUj3oh9NRBv5s6zkeMvMZ2vohGPO-hTBM=415) attracted nearly 20,000 spectators to Baltimore City and the State of Maryland, as the week-long celebration honored Maryland's deep-rooted equestrian history while also embracing the culture, community, and economic vitality of the state.
Inspired by the First Lady's vision to drive more inclusive economic growth and uplift local communities—the festival centered around five major events and numerous co-branded events leading to the 150th running of the Preakness Stakes. The festival was a successful public, private, and non-profit partnership that also expanded opportunities for small minority-owned businesses and hundreds of volunteers.
The Preakness Festival builds on the Moore-Miller administration's commitment to Maryland's equine industry and Baltimore City. The administration invested $400 million into a project that will transform Pimlico Race Course into a year-round hub of economic activity, support hundreds of jobs, drive the creation of a new best-in-class training facility; and bring economic growth, workforce development, and housing to the surrounding Park Heights community.
Maryland’s horse industry generates around $3 billion in economic impact every year and supports over 28,000 jobs. The Preakness Festival marks a transformational change in the way Maryland drives economic growth for the future of equestrian events, while carrying forward the legacy of horse racing in Maryland for generations to come.

### [First Lady Moore Reinforces Commitment to Advocating for Children's Mental Health and Health Equity during CareFirst's Week of Equity and Action](https://links-1.govdelivery.com/CL0/https:%2F%2Fwww.flickr.com%2Fphotos%2Fmdgovpics%2Fsets%2F72177720327548533%2F/1/0100019842662f0a-01c93890-317d-416c-9bbd-45f033f84f84-000000/M8RLQprXvKNRExGlvLocDIMO9Z7ePa36MLNbdjOqZxw=415)
First Lady Moore reinforced her commitment to advocating for children's mental health and health equity during a conversation with CareFirst for its "Week of Equity and Action."
Focused on how empathy-driven leadership can create meaningful community impact, the First Lady spoke on how being a mother and wife fuels her work in uplifting Maryland's resources to support children's mental health. The Moore-Miller administration has invested over $1.4 billion towards mental health, including support for parents.
Last year, in partnership with CareFirst, the Foundation for the Preservation of Government House (FPGH), hosted an interactive day of wellness for young people at Government House. Dozens of young Marylanders participated in activities to manage stress, and spoke on panels about the impact of social media with health care providers and educators. The foundation's guiding objectives are to preserve Government House's historical significance by maintaining its structure and restoring its design while making the landmark accessible and inclusive of all Marylanders— deepening community connections and inspiring advocacy.

## [Governor Moore Announces Streamlined Benefits Access for Marylanders Through Maryland Benefits One Application](https://links-1.govdelivery.com/CL0/https:%2F%2Fgovernor.maryland.gov%2Fnews%2Fpress%2Fpages%2Fgovernor-moore-announces-streamlined-benefits-access-for-marylanders-through-maryland-benefits-one-application.aspx/1/0100019842662f0a-01c93890-317d-416c-9bbd-45f033f84f84-000000/j1ZTNejzizikZV_5KJEe-EZN1SQBFsrWk7OO11mC16A=415)
Governor Wes Moore announced the launch of Maryland Benefits One Application, a new mobile-friendly tool that will help eligible Marylanders apply for vital benefits. The application will make it easier to apply for Medicaid, Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP), Temporary Assistance for Needy Families (TANF), Women, Infants, Children (WIC) programming, and energy assistance in a single application from a computer or smartphone. The new streamlined application is available through Maryland Benefits, the State of Maryland’s online benefits access platform. To access the Maryland Benefits One Application, [visit Marylandbenefits.gov](https://links-1.govdelivery.com/CL0/https:%2F%2Fbenefits.maryland.gov%2Fhome%2F%23%2F/1/0100019842662f0a-01c93890-317d-416c-9bbd-45f033f84f84-000000/iBUutJrWpqOQdTWXSgwbHo0mSSWMrSc-suWjGMOqUg4=415).

### [Governor Moore Announces $50 Million in Grant Awards and a New Philanthropic Fund to Support Vacancy Reduction in Baltimore City](https://links-1.govdelivery.com/CL0/https:%2F%2Fgovernor.maryland.gov%2Fnews%2Fpress%2Fpages%2Fgovernor-moore-announces-50-million-in-grant-awards-and-a-new-philanthropic-fund-to-support-vacancy-reduction-in-baltimore-.aspx/1/0100019842662f0a-01c93890-317d-416c-9bbd-45f033f84f84-000000/74Ccdz6F-AUymrfIk8WRHw9Uq6KsRhmgNH_hmK8g5M8=415)
Governor Moore announced $50 million in grant awards to support vacant property reduction efforts in Baltimore City through the [Baltimore Vacants Reinvestment Initiative](https://links-1.govdelivery.com/CL0/https:%2F%2Fdhcd.maryland.gov%2FReinvest-Baltimore%2FPages%2FBVRI.aspx/1/0100019842662f0a-01c93890-317d-416c-9bbd-45f033f84f84-000000/wuq8RvW8fJhliBa3QAZ_JvborCE3SG-4lDPNcEcduYc=415). The governor also announced a new Baltimore Vacants Reinvestment Initiative Support Fund, toward which philanthropic partners have contributed more than $1 million for technical assistance to support awardees. The announcements marks an acceleration of the Moore-Miller Administration’s commitment to addressing the challenge of vacant properties in Baltimore City neighborhoods [announced last year through the creation of Reinvest Baltimore](https://links-1.govdelivery.com/CL0/https:%2F%2Fgovernor.maryland.gov%2Fnews%2Fpress%2Fpages%2Fgovernor-moore-signs-executive-order-to-maximize-economic-potential-for-neighborhoods-in-baltimore-city.aspx/1/0100019842662f0a-01c93890-317d-416c-9bbd-45f033f84f84-000000/aNW6A58PJjAHF1aTmQoHhUDO5UGIbJPlImVLl1tPsqI=415).

## [](https://links-1.govdelivery.com/CL0/https:%2F%2Fgovernor.maryland.gov%2Fnews%2Fpress%2Fpages%2Fgovernor-moore-announces-additional-action-to-close-maryland%25e2%2580%2599s-racial-wealth-gap-by-promoting-just-community-investment-and.aspx/2/0100019842662f0a-01c93890-317d-416c-9bbd-45f033f84f84-000000/jdWIFsOgPti5qjDlXZkDV1wzJUtpAMe9zGdRRa0awCo=415)[Governor Moore Announces Additional Action to Close Maryland’s Racial Wealth Gap by Promoting Just Community Investment and Expanding Cannabis Pardons](https://links-1.govdelivery.com/CL0/https:%2F%2Fgovernor.maryland.gov%2Fnews%2Fpress%2Fpages%2Fgovernor-moore-announces-additional-action-to-close-maryland%25e2%2580%2599s-racial-wealth-gap-by-promoting-just-community-investment-and.aspx/3/0100019842662f0a-01c93890-317d-416c-9bbd-45f033f84f84-000000/HxnrJLPed8VbFMktCwSgT-aNbT4KhN5WSHGi4ZQC5Lw=415)
On Juneteenth, Governor Moore announced additional action to close the racial wealth gap and expand access to work, wages, and wealth for Black Marylanders. Before a congregation of 200 at Bethel AME Church in Cambridge, the governor made official new Just Community designations to prioritize up to $400 million in competitive state investments in communities that have been historically impacted by exclusionary policies. The governor also announced the addition of nearly 7,000 pardons for certain cannabis convictions, expanding upon the [historic clemency order](https://links-1.govdelivery.com/CL0/https:%2F%2Fgovernor.maryland.gov%2Fnews%2Fpress%2Fpages%2Fgovernor-moore-signs-nationally-historic-executive-order-pardoning-175000-maryland-cannabis-convictions.aspx/1/0100019842662f0a-01c93890-317d-416c-9bbd-45f033f84f84-000000/-tvm_raLP6eaLhYwEP-qG6wFOs8SICNBf-Zy0vme1Ew=415) that the governor signed last year.

I’ve been reminded again and again of what makes Maryland so special—our people. This season has been about lifting others as we lead. As an administration, we've worked to grow our economy, uplift communities that have been historically disenfranchised, support our people during crisis, and partner with the General Assembly to pass legislation to move our state forward. This is the impact we continue to make as we keep our promise to leave no one behind. I can’t wait for what’s ahead and working with all Marylanders to make it happen. Thank you for being on this journey with me. Trump, Collins, and this MAGA Congress have one goal here: Destroy the VA, replace it with privatized health care, and make a quick buck off of sick Veterans.
#
Peter — cutting right to the chase today.
[**We need you to chip in so we can continue working against the Trump administration’s attacks on the VA. If you can, please send $20, $10, even $5.**](https://act.votevets.org/go/2927?c0=vv-pac-em-july25.sScHXv&refcode=em250725-1-120&t=1&akid=34491%2E3013755%2EYBQuth)
We’re asking you today because we’ve seen a real dip in our fundraising over the last month — and because with so many big stories in the news, real threats to the VA are falling under the radar.
We know they’ve already finalized plans that will reduce VA staffing by 30,000 at a time when they are already understaffed and under-resourced. We know VA hospitals and clinics are already suffering from previous cuts. But Trump’s not stopping there.
Republicans in Congress are working on eliminating bonuses for VA staff. It’s a blatant effort to get more of them to quit, and to undermine recruitment for additional talented staff.
Trump’s DOGE boys are using AI to deny valid disability claims, too — an explicit attack on Veterans who need help.
And behind the scenes, VA appointees are working to provide more “choice” for VA patients. “Choice” is a funny word for it, because it actually means destroying internal capacity at the VA in favor of privatization. Never mind the fact that study after study shows Veterans less satisfied with private care than internal VA care.
Trump, Collins, and this MAGA Congress have one goal here: Destroy the VA, replace it with privatized health care, and make a quick buck off of sick Veterans.
Not if we have anything to say about it. VoteVets has stopped every effort to privatize the VA, and we’re not about to quit now.
[**Please, make a donation of anything you can afford so we have the resources we need to spread the word and mobilize against Trump and his lapdogs. They want to destroy the care millions of Veterans depend on. We can’t let that happen.**](https://act.votevets.org/go/2927?c0=vv-pac-em-july25.sScHXv&refcode=em250725-1-120&t=2&akid=34491%2E3013755%2EYBQuth)

Four years ago this week, founding CEO Kadida Kenner was featured in the Philadelphia Inquirer article, "Is the Stacey Abrams method the only hope for saving democracy in Pa.?" by Will Bunch.Today, Will reflects on the state of our democracy and our path forward.

"Kadida Kenner and the New Pennsylvania Project are hoping to copy how Stacey Abrams saved democracy in Georgia by finding lots of new voters."

"Every time I look back on columns from just four years ago, I’m amazed at what a hopeful time that the early days of the Joe Biden presidency felt like, with COVID-19 restrictions fading away and the now quaint notion that the 2020 election had been an upward pivot point for democracy."

"One example of this was an initiative called the New Pennsylvania Project, which was modeled after the wildly successful voter turnout campaigns in Georgia and run by a fiery activist, Kadida Kenner.

“Without new voting rights laws, turnout-boosting schemes like the New Pennsylvania Project might not only be the Democrats’ best shot, but its only path.”

subject: I’ve made my decision

body:
Today, far too many families are working harder than ever and falling further behind — not because they’ve changed but because America has.

Friend, I grew up in a blue-collar family in Oregon, first in the small town of Myrtle Creek, then Roseburg, and, ultimately, East Multnomah County — towns where families worked hard and looked out for each other. My dad worked as a union millwright at the local timber mill, and, thanks to union wages and public schools, I became the first in my family to graduate from college. My story is supposed to be the American story: that with hard work and community support, every child has a chance to succeed. **But today, far too many families are working harder than ever and falling further behind — not because they’ve changed but because America has.** Billionaires and giant corporations have rigged the rules to benefit themselves, dodging taxes and driving up costs while working families struggle to keep up. And Donald Trump? He’s making it worse: more tax breaks for billionaires, handouts to corporate polluters, and dangerous authoritarian policies that undermine our “We the People” republic. It doesn’t have to be this way. We can build an America where families thrive and billionaires finally pay their fair share, where opportunity is real, and the future doesn’t just belong to those at the top. **As Illinoisans prepare for the new school year, the Trump Administration is withholding nearly $218 MILLION in critical funding for education in our state.**

It’s not controversial: Our students deserve fully funded schools. These are resources they need to succeed, for our state to succeed, and our country to succeed.

It’s appalling that our leaders would rather hand out millions in tax breaks to their billionaire donors than fund our public schools – especially in rural areas that need it the most.

This isn’t the only attack on education we’re facing. The Supreme Court has greenlit Trump’s plan to dismantle the Department of Education.

I want you to know that I’m fighting every day in Congress for education – because it’s the backbone of our country. Kids deserve a chance to succeed in every school district and tax bracket.

name: Lindsey Graham
subject: The American Dream isn’t just a slogan.
body:
This is my story, but it’s not so different for many Americans. |
---
I want to share something from the heart with you, Peter.

**_My story._**
It isn't one of glitz and glamour -- it's about hard work, loss, and fighting for what's right. I'm reaching out to tell you why I'm in this fight for our future, and why I need you with me.

Neither of my parents finished high school. But they were hardworking and determined that their children would surpass their achievements.

Most of my growing up happened on the main street of a small textile mill town. My parents had a business establishment -- a combination beer joint, restaurant, liquor store, and pool hall -- known as the Sanitary Cafe right on Main Street in Central, SC. We all lived in the back of the bar where we worked late into the evening, especially my mom, before heading off to bed in the backroom.

[](http://links.freedomtrainalert.com/u/click?_t=2d4f229f156142619b4e4f956d2d65c9&_m=4c5ec23468c24d98bf408c77937dd72a&_e=bAXOER5ZtrI4Kq231Wsnx2Z3cvzEtlKC2cLNyWHfL4YE3OjEuuerhdoBJqaT0JH_OGbPHHNgDSKz-e7wq_7fJcgEwDbLP4y9yNfVGPN7nXp6IiQorN1DgZqTN_fUmbx4yUDrtjYJM-W-9BlwaJTqRcxeyvSbfqiXw9lGaUp9Hu4ulVYlSEwTEHLUUS_imWvwLaSaz-r6alJRdK4II8e7efQ_iEGNBAMZDeEFs795MYw44i1QuQlZj4gnul6FrJn8fuKHOpqxWHQm7-qSAYlg77y0TOaYbU5ak5iaQndDUH0XZkrjAdk_WMGoHtNZuV7_bfqUydmt3w1NC5rsVn9Q5JyJUMD3DSt4T0dECTHK5sXFCLX9Ru6Qpj3tkytP_fIwoS0FxWh1W8GIy_Our4so8qlR5jrI7Z3cUUY1SEx2gkXMGjMGu5EgPslXb5Hs45KM9z3dVYe0LBTQjs8okuffce50maZt5Tu2oKURF7UhB71HpF8vy7T7UAZetvn4D5FSonceHfR60M8a57Yxacn-XGf-aXyFAszs405FslWktFtfZCIL7C2SDU5II7CKoRi711d-P5GxRePZHaTDAlx5UURHWjRDo-d5EvmwKNYHY29_e7eCmVTCj_lnqWb-jB6o8ru50eMri5F6chAimmSUf72E2FNQZW2Ej6KlVZd7eTkHeH9P4TF5kY_rGr0BCrQrhy_u6voFvWna5lJBOdKBDg%3D%3D) I had no silver spoon in my mouth but I never felt I was missing out on something because I didn't live in a house like my friends did. I had a great life, and it was a great way to grow up.

I was the first in my family to attend college, but then life hit me hard. While I was in school, I lost my mom and dad within two years of each other. And just like that, I stepped up to help raise my 13-year-old sister, Darline, while coming back home on the weekends to help at our family business.

[](http://links.freedomtrainalert.com/u/click?_t=2d4f229f156142619b4e4f956d2d65c9&_m=4c5ec23468c24d98bf408c77937dd72a&_e=bAXOER5ZtrI4Kq231Wsnx2Z3cvzEtlKC2cLNyWHfL4YE3OjEuuerhdoBJqaT0JH_OGbPHHNgDSKz-e7wq_7fJcgEwDbLP4y9yNfVGPN7nXp6IiQorN1DgZqTN_fUmbx4yUDrtjYJM-W-9BlwaJTqRcxeyvSbfqiXw9lGaUp9Hu4ulVYlSEwTEHLUUS_imWvwLaSaz-r6alJRdK4II8e7efQ_iEGNBAMZDeEFs795MYw44i1QuQlZj4gnul6FrJn8kqa0L4yl1EEf2E8wVfqRBP3cIKYn8GfGxt_UoTN4lZxl45WpBN8z8_sJPxAgtuZ2N2wAARMgYqTnjeLUFych8odbTomfUOvbAP3BJIbESQCKjl_XGHITW_hG9KqP5Wrzj_FZx-GFsIlzNUtlLOZIXdHFOJTSs6WRYgjUtZDq9qc31t3GDhQV1Uqb-Ac07_1xl54Pk5RiaEpbw-Xmms8zsPc7fKnk7Onx5w5K7BQqlj7TaRxYMxdDDyBPCxNPIRTxBk-CSJbkJvXz47axY6-ffHC3JdBWj8s7nXpk_9HspiwQiyIEoDRg-I6WNEPQin1MVRj0cUfzzF05vP5SUw_60dOTviDrLMiqbAxvITFJ4xsLHAgHZtuicMtGMtoySGr3AlvhvbYLX_Y2KuM5W2LBmEzu6PV-g1RqHEoUzxaL6C_U18ypVstN6hNn4HW648n9T3YGAiRamioBFcTMOZ87RA%3D%3D) **Peter, I learned some tough lessons early on.**

After law school, I joined the U.S. Air Force as a Judge Advocate General, serving as a military prosecutor and defense attorney. Even after the people of South Carolina sent me to the United States Senate, I continued my service in the Air Force Reserves. I performed several short deployments in war zones like Afghanistan and Iraq, standing shoulder to shoulder with our brave men and women in uniform.

My story isn't all that different from yours or most people across this great country. I didn't have anything handed to me. I worked hard, grew up quickly, and took on big responsibilities.

**But what shaped me most was listening to the hard -working South Carolinians who'd come by our family business, sharing their hopes and struggles, or hearing the perspectives of my brave colleagues in the military.** _Whether I agreed with them or not, those conversations built my understanding of what Americans need and deserve._

Now, Peter, we all know our nation's in a tough spot -- we're divided, but there are some things we should agree on, plain and simple.

**🇺🇸 We need a country where you can raise your family without fear, where the streets are safe.**
**🇺🇸 We need a country where the American Dream isn't just a slogan.**
_It's alive, and every hard -working American has a real shot at it, no matter where they start._
**[That's what I'm fighting for every single day, Peter.](http://links.freedomtrainalert.com/u/click?_t=2d4f229f156142619b4e4f956d2d65c9&_m=4c5ec23468c24d98bf408c77937dd72a&_e=bAXOER5ZtrI4Kq231Wsnx2Z3cvzEtlKC2cLNyWHfL4YE3OjEuuerhdoBJqaT0JH_OGbPHHNgDSKz-e7wq_7fJcgEwDbLP4y9yNfVGPN7nXp6IiQorN1DgZqTN_fUmbx4yUDrtjYJM-W-9BlwaJTqRcxeyvSbfqiXw9lGaUp9Hu4ulVYlSEwTEHLUUS_imWvwLaSaz-r6alJRdK4II8e7efQ_iEGNBAMZDeEFs795MYw44i1QuQlZj4gnul6FrJn8lvahPg5W4IUk2Jw7QtTms913Mq_OLusascj1l4r1QNrOQQuPJUQsieqsIcKpH48sz48LzADlYZ3jiUIp9o76BbUjI1h2CS8XgIWL42WW-AYMk6BpTRNQ-PJXfj8yOVHgkFvslFKJlGELhUSUXfUvBwwhWj41-KKmcInEI6BClZOZiUqalk73n5XdFP-JgI32ltiBaZI8aB_e8VIjCq3ncKf3xE5UWjUTjr3vQdHqaisbS9_aA9KN224WHWEY1rfgY8hp6Bmz0HxHuk41gUxLtRtRQQSsRDsJB6x3qhw8xNoOleJhUSA5CAKvGYJg8bJuDOFlEd-wsVkgto2AeXsUlPkdl9j040mUXY71LEyhuC0czNmQdACE1qb_coBgVZJOFuPN3oq5eRRxNxtJ0eo1P6AAkoDn8zZs3_Qdg8FadLdpyCViSf3pgFm1tyHJ24tz4p0CDzHfaZEwSW6lVvIpbg%3D%3D)**

Sadly, there are folks in Washington, across the aisle, who don't see it that way. They're fine with open borders, allowing violent crime spill into our neighborhoods. They're okay with slapping higher taxes on hard-working folks like you, piling more burdens on your family. That isn't right, and I won't stand for it.

clean_body: This is my story, but it’s not so different for many Americans. | I want to share something from the heart with you, Peter. My story. It isn't one of glitz and glamour -- it's about hard work, loss, and fighting for what's right. I'm reaching out to tell you why I'm in this fight for our future, and why I need you with me. Neither of my parents finished high school. But they were hardworking and determined that their children would surpass their achievements. Most of my growing up happened on the main street of a small textile mill town. My parents had a business establishment -- a combination beer joint, restaurant, liquor store, and pool hall -- known as the Sanitary Cafe right on Main Street in Central, SC. We all lived in the back of the bar where we worked late into the evening, especially my mom, before heading off to bed in the backroom. I had no silver spoon in my mouth but I never felt I was missing out on something because I didn't live in a house like my friends did. I had a great life, and it was a great way to grow up. I was the first in my family to attend college, but then life hit me hard. While I was in school, I lost my mom and dad within two years of each other. And just like that, I stepped up to help raise my 13-year-old sister, Darline, while coming back home on the weekends to help at our family business. Peter, I learned some tough lessons early on. After law school, I joined the U.S. Air Force as a Judge Advocate General, serving as a military prosecutor and defense attorney. Even after the people of South Carolina sent me to the United States Senate, I continued my service in the Air Force Reserves. I performed several short deployments in war zones like Afghanistan and Iraq, standing shoulder to shoulder with our brave men and women in uniform. My story isn't all that different from yours or most people across this great country. I didn't have anything handed to me. I worked hard, grew up quickly, and took on big responsibilities. But what shaped me most was listening to the hard -working South Carolinians who'd come by our family business, sharing their hopes and struggles, or hearing the perspectives of my brave colleagues in the military. Whether I agreed with them or not, those conversations built my understanding of what Americans need and deserve. Now, Peter, we all know our nation's in a tough spot -- we're divided, but there are some things we should agree on, plain and simple. 🇺🇸 We need a country where you can raise your family without fear, where the streets are safe. 🇺🇸 We need a country where the American Dream isn't just a slogan. It's alive, and every hard -working American has a real shot at it, no matter where they start. Sadly, there are folks in Washington, across the aisle, who don't see it that way. They're fine with open borders, allowing violent crime spill into our neighborhoods. They're okay with slapping higher taxes on hard-working folks like you, piling more burdens on your family. That isn't right, and I won't stand for it. So I'm coming to you with a simple ask, Peter. If you've got a few dollars to spare, | Peter, I know we can build a country that keeps our communities safe, rewards hard work, and gives every American a chance to chase their dreams -- just like I did. Friend, it’s Michael.
Since I launched this campaign, I’ve been listening to Coloradans in every corner and community across our great state.
The dream of owning your own home feels out of reach. Childcare and healthcare costs keep going up. Small businesses are struggling to deal with Trump’s incompetent economics, and consumers are fronting the bill.
These are just some of the genuine concerns I’ve been hearing.
It’s clear that Trump’s chaos and Washington’s broken politics will not deliver us any real solutions. So we’ll just have to do the work ourselves.
It’s exactly why I’m running for Colorado Governor. I know the solutions that we desperately need will come from us at home, working together to get big things done.
You’ll be a key part of that, friend. If you have a second, I’d love to hear from you. My campaign is conducting a Colorado Priorities survey to hear about the concerns and issues facing your life. [https://secure.michaelbennet.com/a/colorado-priorities-survey-mbsend]

clean_body: [] Friend, it’s Michael. Since I launched this campaign, I’ve been listening to Coloradans in every corner and community across our great state. The dream of owning your own home feels out of reach. Childcare and healthcare costs keep going up. Small businesses are struggling to deal with Trump’s incompetent economics, and consumers are fronting the bill. These are just some of the genuine concerns I’ve been hearing. It’s clear that Trump’s chaos and Washington’s broken politics will not deliver us any real solutions. So we’ll just have to do the work ourselves. It’s exactly why I’m running for Colorado Governor. I know the solutions that we desperately need will come from us at home, working together to get big things done. You’ll be a key part of that, friend. If you have a second, I’d love to hear from you. My campaign is conducting a Colorado Priorities survey to hear about the concerns and issues facing your life. [] COLORADO PRIORITIES SURVEY [] Hearing from you is invaluable to me. Peter, As president, I was often inspired by a quote from Dr. Martin Luther King, Jr.: "The arc of the moral universe is long, but it bends toward justice." The line is well-known for a reason: it’s a north star for all of us who are committed to the pursuit of progress. But people sometimes forget the first part: "_The arc of the moral universe is long" _— so long that sometimes you can’t see it bend. Sometimes it zigs. Sometimes it zags. There are periods of progress followed by times of reversal. But while victories don’t come easily, it’s also true that setbacks aren’t final – so long as we don’t let the forces of injustice have the last word. And of course, the arc doesn’t bend on its own. As my friend and our former Attorney General Eric Holder likes to say, “It only bends when people like us put our hands on it and pull it toward justice.” I tried to bend the arc as president, but the job didn’t end when I left the Oval Office. Each of us has a critical role to play as citizens to bend it, too – including you, Peter. **That’s why Eric and I launched the National Democratic Redistricting Committee in the first place. And with your support, it’s leading the fight against gerrymandering so voters can choose their representatives instead of the other way around.** [**I’m grateful that my friends at the NDRC have been able to count on your support. Now, as we face escalating threats to free and fair elections, I’m asking you to step up again with a donation of $30.**](https://click.everyaction.com/k/112128007/559490177/-1066425169?refcode=don_ndrc_tier1_email_ObamaJuly_email_20250725-NDRC-Tier1-ObamaJuly_&utm_source=email&utm_medium=email&utm_term=don&utm_content=20250725-NDRC-Tier1-ObamaJuly_&utm_campaign=ObamaJuly&amount=30&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9FQS9FQTAxMy8xLzg5Mjk0IiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogImUyMGM2M2U4LTdhNjktZjAxMS04ZGM5LTYwNDViZGE5ZDk2YiIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=UrvRncQHsA30Mm870gHR8J_Y-1RwmpbYdpR1_JOwqM8=) | _If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will go through immediately:_

After years of serving as the strategic hub against gerrymandering, the NDRC has helped make sure the latest congressional maps are the fairest in decades.
But it’s not guaranteed to stay that way. Right now, too many people in power are actively trying to make our democracy less fair — to roll back fair maps and limit voting rights. Just this month, Republicans announced a sudden, mid-decade plan to redraw Texas’ already-gerrymandered congressional map — a transparent power grab they publicly say could win them up to five seats in the midterms.
That’s why the NDRC is keeping up the fight. They’re helping elect fair maps champions in the races that have the biggest effect on the state-by-state redistricting process — and key elections are happening _this year._ They’re holding the line against new attempts to consolidate unearned power by manipulating district lines. And they’re keeping this issue that touches every other element of our fight for a stronger democracy front and center.
In other words, this team is playing the long game. Because that’s what it takes to bend the arc of history.
**Every time you speak out against rising threats to democracy, you’re doing your part. And every time you make a grassroots donation, you join forces with friends, neighbors, and fellow supporters across the country who are helping build a more just future.**
[**That’s why I’m personally asking you to make a contribution to the NDRC today. With your support, we can keep moving forward on the long journey toward justice.**](https://click.everyaction.com/k/112128014/559490184/-1066425169?refcode=don_ndrc_tier1_email_ObamaJuly_email_20250725-NDRC-Tier1-ObamaJuly_&utm_source=email&utm_medium=email&utm_term=don&utm_content=20250725-NDRC-Tier1-ObamaJuly_&utm_campaign=ObamaJuly&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9FQS9FQTAxMy8xLzg5Mjk0IiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogImUyMGM2M2U4LTdhNjktZjAxMS04ZGM5LTYwNDViZGE5ZDk2YiIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=UrvRncQHsA30Mm870gHR8J_Y-1RwmpbYdpR1_JOwqM8=)

clean_body: Each of us has a role to play in shaping the future of our democracy. | Peter, As president, I was often inspired by a quote from Dr. Martin Luther King, Jr.: "The arc of the moral universe is long, but it bends toward justice." The line is well-known for a reason: it’s a north star for all of us who are committed to the pursuit of progress. But people sometimes forget the first part: "The arc of the moral universe is long" — so long that sometimes you can’t see it bend. Sometimes it zigs. Sometimes it zags. There are periods of progress followed by times of reversal. But while victories don’t come easily, it’s also true that setbacks aren’t final – so long as we don’t let the forces of injustice have the last word. And of course, the arc doesn’t bend on its own. As my friend and our former Attorney General Eric Holder likes to say, “It only bends when people like us put our hands on it and pull it toward justice.” I tried to bend the arc as president, but the job didn’t end when I left the Oval Office. Each of us has a critical role to play as citizens to bend it, too – including you, Peter. That’s why Eric and I launched the National Democratic Redistricting Committee in the first place. And with your support, it’s leading the fight against gerrymandering so voters can choose their representatives instead of the other way around. = | If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will go through immediately: = | = = | = = | = After years of serving as the strategic hub against gerrymandering, the NDRC has helped make sure the latest congressional maps are the fairest in decades. body:
| [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/112128779/559492069/-1623651544?refcode=em-header&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTAvMS8xMDM1MzYiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiMjNhZTRhY2YtN2M2OS1mMDExLThkYzktNjA0NWJkYTlkOTZiIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=mAwjQmlvPYwioPjsyWpS93OfCL2lG6IYflvEQXdvqN0=) Seventeen years ago, I completed my final treatment for breast cancer. I was fortunate: I had access to advanced screenings and treatments that helped save my life. But fortune shouldn’t determine one’s ability to get life-saving cancer treatments. I want to make sure every American has affordable access to care. **That’s why I’m proud to join colleagues in sponsoring the SCREENS for Cancer Act of 2025, which will expand breast and cervical cancer screening and treatment for those who lack access to these important services.** Surviving breast cancer made me realize I couldn’t put off the things I was passionate about, and it made me reevaluate the impact that I could make on the world with whatever time I was privileged enough to have. Part of that impact is removing barriers that prevent too many women — especially those in underserved communities — from getting the screenings that could save their lives. Breast cancer is the second leading cause of cancer death in women. One of every 43 women will succumb to the disease. But we know early discovery reduces the likelihood of overcoming cancer. **And this simple fix could significantly improve the outcomes for millions.** As the first woman ever elected to serve CA-30, I’m honored to fight every day to open more opportunities for all women – in their careers, their economic mobility, and especially in their healthcare. Sometimes I’m working. Sometimes I’m reviewing our budget. Sometimes I’m just lying there staring at the ceiling, thinking about what this country is going to look like if we don’t get it together. I think about how we’re going to pay the bills. I think about the rising cost of groceries, childcare, and housing. I think about my kids and the world they’re inheriting — one shaped by billionaires, corporate monopolies, and a political class that’s more afraid of donors than of losing the soul of this nation. **That’s what keeps me going.** It’s the fear. But it’s also the fire. Because I refuse to sit back while this country slides into full-blown authoritarianism and corporate rule. We’ve got MAGA extremists cheering on mass deportations and ending democracy as we know it. And we’ve got Democratic leadership stuck in the past, offering up polite soundbites while the middle class crumbles. Meanwhile, billionaires and private equity firms are buying up housing, hospitals, farmland, and even our water — like this whole country is just one big asset to be stripped and sold. But I didn’t get into this race to manage our decline. **I’m in it to stop it.** I’m in it to uplift working families. To restore some damn dignity to the people who actually build this country. To make sure our kids don’t grow up in a place where democracy is something they only read about in textbooks. We can’t afford another generation of polished career politicians who play it safe while the system burns. So if you’ve ever stayed up late worrying about the same things... If you’ve ever felt ignored, overlooked, or left behind by a system rigged against you... If you’ve ever wanted to be part of something real — something built from the ground up, by and for working people... This is your campaign. And right now, I need your help. We don’t have corporate PACs or party bosses bankrolling this movement. Every single town hall we host, every trip across the district, every ad we run — it all comes from people like you. We’re taking on the establishment. We’re challenging both parties to do better. And we’re doing it without a machine behind us — just real people who are ready for real change. **[Chip in now to help fuel our campaign and fight for a future worth believing clean_body: | | | Friend, I stay up most nights later than I should. Sometimes I’m working. Sometimes I’m reviewing our budget. Sometimes I’m just lying there staring at the ceiling, thinking about what this country is going to look like if we don’t get it together. I think about how we’re going to pay the bills. I think about the rising cost of groceries, childcare, and housing. I think about my kids and the world they’re inheriting — one shaped by billionaires, corporate monopolies, and a political class that’s more afraid of donors than of losing the soul of this nation. That’s what keeps me going. It’s the fear. But it’s also the fire. Because I refuse to sit back while this country slides into full-blown authoritarianism and corporate rule. We’ve got MAGA extremists cheering on mass deportations and ending democracy as we know it. And we’ve got Democratic leadership stuck in the past, offering up polite soundbites while the middle class crumbles. Meanwhile, billionaires and private equity firms are buying up housing, hospitals, farmland, and even our water — like this whole country is just one big asset to be stripped and sold. But I didn’t get into this race to manage our decline. I’m in it to stop it. I’m in it to uplift working families. To restore some damn dignity to the people who actually build this country. To make sure our kids don’t grow up in a place where democracy is something they only read about in textbooks. We can’t afford another generation of polished career politicians who play it safe while the system burns. So if you’ve ever stayed up late worrying about the same things... If you’ve ever felt ignored, overlooked, or left behind by a system rigged against you... If you’ve ever wanted to be part of something real — something built from the ground up, by and for working people... This is your campaign. And right now, I need your help. We don’t have corporate PACs or party bosses bankrolling this movement. Every single town hall we host, every trip across the district, every ad we run — it all comes from people like you. We’re taking on the establishment. We’re challenging both parties to do better. And we’re doing it without a machine behind us — just real people who are ready for real change. _But as a result, MAGA Republicans are FURIOUS and are RAMPING UP their ATTACKS on Bernie Sanders. They are VOWING to END his career and DERAIL his anti-MAGA agenda!_

FROM: A proud Democrat
Subject: Thank you. Dear Senator Bernie Sanders,

**We are truly grateful to have you speak out against Trump and MAGA Republicans at this crucial time in our nation’s history. As a Senator, you have continued to call out Trump’s lies and his dangerous policies that are pushing our Democracy to the BRINK of authoritarianism.**

You are inspiring Democrats in every part of the country, _and Trump is FURIOUS and SCARED of the grassroots movement you are building._

Now while extremist Republicans ramp up their attacks, you have not backed down. You have stood up for the American people, and we couldn’t be more grateful for your bravery and your courageous leadership.

**Your leadership is absolutely critical right now, and we hope more Democrats follow your lead.**

[**I can’t thank you enough for all of your work to stop Donald Trump and save our Democracy! body:
#
Fox News and the right wing would have you believe that my American values are something out of the communist manifesto.
But I don’t believe in healthcare, labor, and human dignity because I’m an extremist.
**I believe these things because I was a waitress**.
Because I’ve worked double shifts to keep the lights on.
Because I did lose a parent to cancer and I saw my mom open the hospital bill a couple of days later.
Because on my worst day, **I know what it feels like to feel left behind**.
I don’t want any of us to live like this anymore. We deserve better.
But together, we've built a movement that is pushing harder than ever for guaranteed healthcare, bold action on our climate crisis, and so much more.

Fellow activist, There is a court case set to be heard by the U.S. Supreme Court, and we are sounding the alarm:

_Turtle Mountain Band of Chippewa Indians v. Howe_ **could further gut the landmark Voting Rights Act of 1965** , which bans racial discrimination in voting. According to _Vox_ , this lawsuit tries to prohibit private individuals and groups from suing because they’re not explicitly named in the VRA. While the Justice Department could still file suits to challenge racial discrimination in elections if this ruling is upheld, it is currently controlled by Trump, who is actively working to undermine efforts to protect minority groups from bias.

**This case is included in the U.S. Supreme Court’s shadow docket and could be taken up at any point. **

**Here’s the background:** Native American tribes and voters in North Dakota brought a lawsuit in federal court against the state's secretary of state. According to _SCOTUSblog_ , they contended that a state legislative map from 2021 diluted the voting power of Native Americans and violated Section 2 of the VRA because it eliminated two of the three legislative districts in the part of the state where Native American voters could elect their own candidates. A judge ruled that voters cannot use federal civil rights laws to bring lawsuits alleging violations of Section Two, and it’s now heading to the U.S. Supreme Court.

This is just the latest attack on the Voting Rights Act of 1965, and it remains clear: **our courts are as critical as ever before. **
[**With make-or-break judicial elections taking place in PA this year, we need to be prepared. NPP is fighting to ensure that all Pennsylvanians eligible to vote, especially Black, Indigenous, and other people of color, immigrant communities, and young adults (17-35-year-olds), understand what’s at stake and are ready to turn out and make their voices heard. clean_body: | | | Fellow activist, There is a court case set to be heard by the U.S. Supreme Court, and we are sounding the alarm: Turtle Mountain Band of Chippewa Indians v. Howe could further gut the landmark Voting Rights Act of 1965 , which bans racial discrimination in voting. According to Vox , this lawsuit tries to prohibit private individuals and groups from suing because they’re not explicitly named in the VRA. While the Justice Department could still file suits to challenge racial discrimination in elections if this ruling is upheld, it is currently controlled by Trump, who is actively working to undermine efforts to protect minority groups from bias. This case is included in the U.S. Supreme Court’s shadow docket and could be taken up at any point. Here’s the background: Native American tribes and voters in North Dakota brought a lawsuit in federal court against the state's secretary of state. According to SCOTUSblog , they contended that a state legislative map from 2021 diluted the voting power of Native Americans and violated Section 2 of the VRA because it eliminated two of the three legislative districts in the part of the state where Native American voters could elect their own candidates. A judge ruled that voters cannot use federal civil rights laws to bring lawsuits alleging violations of Section Two, and it’s now heading to the U.S. Supreme Court. This is just the latest attack on the Voting Rights Act of 1965, and it remains clear: our courts are as critical as ever before. name: Team WFP
subject: Less than half of Democratic voters approve of Democrats in Congress
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Working Families Party PAC (77 Sands St
body:
This is a warning to any politician who thinks the status quo is acceptable. | | | Peter, The two-party system is failing all of us. And the American people are noticing. In a new Quinnipiac poll, only 33% of voters approve of the job that Congressional Republicans are doing. Just 19% of voters approve of Congressional Democrats. **And only 39% of Democratic voters approve of the job that their _own party_ is doing in Congress, with 52% disapproving.**1 This is a level of discontent within a major party unseen since the Tea Party raged within the GOP more than a decade ago. And it is a warning to any politician who thinks the status quo is at all acceptable. Working people are demanding _more_ from their government. Housing and health care they can afford, jobs that allow a life of dignity — **and leaders with a real vision for our future who know that winning against Trump and Republicans depends on having the courage to fight hard for it.** At the Working Families Party, we organize year-round to build support for an alternative vision to the one offered by the billionaire class. We are building a movement that elects true working class champions into office so they can fight FOR us, not against us. In a new Quinnipiac poll, only 33% of voters approve of the job that Congressional Republicans are doing. Just 19% of voters approve of Congressional Democrats. And only 39% of Democratic voters approve of the job that their own party is doing in Congress, with 52% disapproving.1 This is a level of discontent within a major party unseen since the Tea Party raged within the GOP more than a decade ago. And it is a warning to any politician who thinks the status quo is at all acceptable. Working people are demanding more from their government. Housing and health care they can afford, jobs that allow a life of dignity — and leaders with a real vision for our future who know that winning against Trump and Republicans depends on having the courage to fight hard for it. body:
For decades, the governor’s seat has flipped from blue to red, red to blue — every two terms.
# [](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/133?t=1&akid=3393%2E400544%2E-6RuTa)
New Mexico has a pattern.
For _decades_ , the governor’s seat has flipped from blue to red, red to blue — every two terms.
Now, with an outgoing Democratic governor, this seat is open, and Republicans are betting history will repeat itself. And the truth is: **if we don’t act, they could be right.**
I’m already facing right-wing attacks, and we’re hearing that a millionaire Republican with the ability to self-fund his campaign could jump into this already crowded and expensive race at any moment.
**But here’s what I know: New Mexico voters are fiercer than any pattern. Together we can buck this trend by building a powerful movement rooted in our shared values.**
I’m running for governor to put New Mexicans first, protect our public lands, and ensure every family — no matter their zip code — has the tools they need to thrive. But I can’t do it alone.
**[So I’m asking: can you pitch in $5, or whatever you can, before to help build a historic grassroots campaign and keep New Mexico blue? This week, I successfully [got a motion through](http://links.burchettforcongress.com/s/c/I8yf7diwXNik3yvpZqYWEX_P1yGoYRTrCPnTJMMwT3JZP8wRmDnIs7tB4a8BmqvuE8kcU9y1rODUVS-jaZd2dkTFk0rL7TaaCNgdOAysARURh3y2e3180QbtTWBkKwZfZszF1ctnkRr4PEcB89boMiYmgL-fLDViTJApgugUw4kYiOOqQGJea4lVApFxOrh8imVA2pY32s7ohOa5oS-Z5h1idSZYQTEGEuX0cKsDEPhXC4-mICnhArsz_yop8icOaRvu5o1MzVCWdxDfQENUgJDzdvhYxyXkjLXNUlbC5WRDH9N2QhUJRiwb16qbqhnw4CCnd2EzHACMUKh4a24G3NJ8EJMn5aVGTD1Njl5Vxjm14cS9ysa8csYW7Zb44Rak49h-OyVD8MEzr7EZy6P0S1UwRA/N5aXn7GLNhrN2B10EHNB45PeroiEToBE/11) to subpoena Ghislaine Maxwell for a deposition. It’s kinda like a court hearing, but behind closed doors—and she has to tell the truth or she’ll be in a world of trouble with the law. The motion [passed](http://links.burchettforcongress.com/s/c/n4lYHmdSOLuo4XBDQIja56A-lXjlqi04vQPMWCUyjA4cSTfnN-90N2TAC3VB7dMNGjFQ55qYtFFRCk5kyZ9Xe1aSK3ZRCpvHRZ1y4RpD7El8l_aG0289qrWDUbrUAmWqTn1RGlom-nVB9cARV15H52nNFXqnXFVmpmvQbiUxCdYDstNBKUjvfw8DQMNgOYbyoCWdaD5wj4T-Ak0tisVO0P3diCTjEUpGr6UAvNRI9ncWc3T4WDNoQfWrOvTCkkvuilovRCSSuNWT5iFgA8_ww6Qfz671WuUDkjGmFTE3ISCSpFhGT2NblEuy73XrL3AeFPcI703QNhkOtLgY8oqTpA5UHDgB1O3KSeWrRzD7WmMFaHa0bcm-R4LXprADKPV7SWLFHSTAMq8CmjgepnnsFgIMYEnshJ1ghoXSnBveDVqSyM9VqofSCxrwuFvOeDRJgNBlkl9k-Fl9Dx5TWEBlFQcFj9PYizdUhfs-v3KoAjW3Knu9wEk2yNQuDiWS_JCPn2AypQl6IZgc/Bjfl7nvEdNxVV8RZ8d2TmFa2inpRKA4Q/11) the Government Operations Subcommittee without a single “no” vote, which doesn’t happen much in this town. If all goes according to plan, Epstein’s partner in crime will be in the hot seat on [August 11](http://links.burchettforcongress.com/s/c/P_c45YKFQ_dfThYBJEoqXsDq2IHPRTqprewmhgc_HJZumwRfhunI10o10qHGVWFiC3RIVfVtx4j-SNSxu11FlDMO36bpVa1Dr3nU1rKf_i3rEpwpdZd5DavWXnwmo7uanY0C-ziHTPOME7BMwr4fobFZuZZ1HaP_P1rYUVKEKvqqXXH3xHZ82P1zCNwZEn_SqfGJYti_lC2ae2Xj4Ff02z-G5oztUKayw2sZwkFNgww3AgV2O4etnXvcDBeR_ZMsnxVi2gMgYjE6QORReQSZioCN00CVSRsOA4R7HUkKnbX0torbr-sy3YBZbHevlzWPSIodOysbgK2CVB11ST4Oa_EiLjfg6W7KXCzEtRnzg5hMGNaqPPCmFAToLf171PfL-Zfwhtb7u2MhnHSTko-b8FFqblgqjLz8UGGpOEoMa9-LR85NczP382F8gT-kgLiixwoVtVDe6oBcUCVH1TocbIhCQb4ftylrLs_SFDBLWDRnxjTxK015RzI5GodbpzXLjmP4R_3k33oaSGzIADxMILlPZwWLrNlR6Ulph_Svnmye/d7fkdRxQi5eSLVE3qUcF2RT3CD-N5wk_/11) at the prison down in Tallahassee. I know I sound like a broken record, but we still don’t have the answers we deserve—and that’s why this deposition is so important. Do I think every name found in those pages is a criminal? Of course not. Folks with a lot of money want to fly on private jets and hang out with the rich and famous. We all know that. But let’s not kid ourselves—there will be some truly filthy dirtbags sprinkled in there. Ghislaine knows exactly who they are and what they did, so it’s time for her to do some talking. She can lay out just how deep Epstein’s criminal network ran, who helped cover it up, and how they got away with this evil [for so long](http://links.burchettforcongress.com/s/c/bQNvOiDrcKeqPOnfsj42k9Brmb3o7VyGOLNpgP8EvC4quKgpt4D3VdMJvK7QiZjAWNbBzz4nOm2_Fva5os2VQyve5DEsJcUue2RBvGrjbV7zmtE6k4wzMUV64A8xeFaTPZtCKMXgLQHMDEyL5d-4l76xmiplpaGEw8_s5wI98jcrpM4v3NR-d9DbAx5SiWAbKFwKKeGBP_DLEUcCxyZt-gfsQmZrpTWe1jfF0_yaLYs7kJcj5ufXEdm13Cx1aP9ywoRI738pd5t_gx7EcUghwHkqe5SV_Z2e08Gzg07xrhrV2t078QHtdf2dDwnEV-Hw-BKLNKDIU4w1FdyHB6Tj48vY6HqCruLpQweNCJ1p5S7mKH1-Nh7a3KtdOUTDuS-0zKQP3DbEJyE29wJhhrn7T_pYjg4_gGElXceZDyKOfeziP-2T5qsUhZp-HYoM5CkoZ5bdzsSmWclqpNhQDbyW1B1CVUqkgRXdyc1iHBFdZRr3FVKVzaEBMky3Nq-PPpKhpG_m26E/LGPmFLjOAZXP4JFO5KjqxGPDgtKn0qwa/11). And I also want to know how on earth they accessed the poor young people they violated. Do I think we’ll ever get the full truth? Probably not. Washington doesn’t give up its secrets without a fight. But God knows I’m fighting too—and this is a step in the right direction. This is about transparency, accountability, and JUSTICE. We owe it to the victims and to the American people to keep pushing until we get some answers.

| Letter from the Chair
---
Time to Refocus
Time flies when you're busy, and it's been four months since I was elected Chairman of the NEGOP. We've come a long way, and quite a bit has been accomplished during the transition. I immersed myself in learning the finances, making appointments to leadership, forming and filling committees, and adding staff where needed. Our Political Director and I continued the execution of the political plan and have been meeting with potential candidates and campaign managers. During the transition, Republicans did not fare as well as we would have hoped in the Lincoln or Omaha city races. Lessons have been learned.
Along the way, I've enjoyed the opportunities to talk to previous Chairmen and Executive Directors about their tenures in office. They've been generous in sharing their time and offering their advice. Each story told to me completes a piece of the puzzle of the history of Nebraska politics. Each faced challenges unique to the time and the circumstances, and I am not alone.
The future is bright for the Nebraska Republican Party. We will refocus our efforts and look forward to building relationships and communicating the values of the Republican Party that work to protect life, strengthen families, grow the economy, expand energy sources, and build the good life for all Nebraskans. If you have considered running for office, and would like to talk about it, please call or email. There are open seats at all levels of government, and we're determined that they be filled by Republicans. Let us all join in refocusing our efforts on that goal.

Mary Jane Truemper Chairman, Nebraska Republican Party

With the 2026 primary filing deadline less than a year away, the Nebraska Republican Party is charging full speed ahead, recruiting candidates for more than 450 offices across the state. clean_body: News, events, and action items to keep Nebraska red and growing strong. | | | | | | Letter from the Chair Time to Refocus Time flies when you're busy, and it's been four months since I was elected Chairman of the NEGOP. We've come a long way, and quite a bit has been accomplished during the transition. I immersed myself in learning the finances, making appointments to leadership, forming and filling committees, and adding staff where needed. Our Political Director and I continued the execution of the political plan and have been meeting with potential candidates and campaign managers. During the transition, Republicans did not fare as well as we would have hoped in the Lincoln or Omaha city races. Lessons have been learned. Along the way, I've enjoyed the opportunities to talk to previous Chairmen and Executive Directors about their tenures in office. They've been generous in sharing their time and offering their advice. Each story told to me completes a piece of the puzzle of the history of Nebraska politics. Each faced challenges unique to the time and the circumstances, and I am not alone. The future is bright for the Nebraska Republican Party. We will refocus our efforts and look forward to building relationships and communicating the values of the Republican Party that work to protect life, strengthen families, grow the economy, expand energy sources, and build the good life for all Nebraskans. If you have considered running for office, and would like to talk about it, please call or email. There are open seats at all levels of government, and we're determined that they be filled by Republicans. Let us all join in refocusing our efforts on that goal. Mary Jane Truemper Chairman, Nebraska Republican Party | | | | What's Happening... The issue of gun violence is what brought me to public service. When I was just a kid in McKeesport, an incident of gun violence in my neighborhood spurred me into a lifetime of public service.
I knew I had to do everything in my power to prevent what happened to my community from happening again and make sure families of victims receive the support they need.
**I believe it's possible to end gun violence. Our communities deserve to be safe. No family should have to go through what I witnessed in McKeesport, and I fight for that every day.**
With common-sense gun safety legislation and targeted investments in public education and community programming, we will create a better, safer future for the next generation so that they can thrive here in PA and beyond.
[**It’s my honor and privilege to be in this fight. Beth Van Duyne is running for Congress because she knows the people of the 24th District deserve to have a strong, principled voice in Congress. She's been asked what prompted her to run for public office; the answer is simple – her children. We live in a very fragile time for our nation, our families, and the future of the American Dream. Socialism is on the rise, our border crisis has never been worse, and we face constant threats from hostile nations willing to use cyber-attacks, nuclear weapons, and terrorist jihad. When Beth thinks about her two children, she wants them to have the same opportunities in life that she did; She wants them to be able to grow up safe and proud of our country. Beth is a single mom, a conservative Republican, a reformer who has defeated government corruption, a believer in the rule of law** who has helped remove thousands of criminal aliens from North Texas, a leader who helped deliver growth and new job opportunities, and a Constitutionalist who has never backed down when it comes to protecting the rights of all North Texans. | PAID FOR BY BETH VAN DUYNE FOR CONGRESS
