name: Heidi Campbell
subject: Interrogating The Machine
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Campbell for State Senate, Lee Jones, treasurer
body:
https://voteheidicampbell.com/ [https://voteheidicampbell.com/]
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/NGP/NGP10/1/81515/images/a569b8e2-907e-47f6-951d-3f1c9dfbc691_300x168.png]
I’m not a fan of AI writing for us—if you’ve read my work, you know that I think it’s a slippery slope. The risks are massive, the rewards uncertain, and the people wielding the tools? Mostly unregulated tech billionaires. And it’s also cheating, and probably bad for our health (don’t ask me how- it just must be).
But I do think there’s value in interrogating the tool itself. And that’s what I did.
Why share this? Because tools like this are going to shape elections, write our laws, and inform our beliefs. It would appear as if we can (to some degree) interrogate them now—on our terms—since this seems to be the early, participatory phase of the system’s evolution, where the illusion of agency is preserved, before those who control the technology begin to shape the questions, steer the narratives, and quietly define the limits of what can be asked—or imagined. ( Do I sound paranoid? )
We’re living in a bizarre time of fragmented, conflicting perceptions of reality, shaped by algorithms, curated outrage, and collapsing trust in institutions. AI isn’t neutral in that landscape. It mirrors our collective confusion, our blind spots, and our power structures—while offering the illusion of objectivity.
That’s why it makes sense to query the machine. Not to get some divine truth, but to see how AI interprets the chaos we’ve created—and to trace the outlines of the stories it tells us about ourselves. If this technology is going to shape how we think, vote, teach, and govern, we should interrogate it early and often.
Not just the tech bros, but the artists, teachers, skeptics, and citizens.
This is one such interrogation (to be read in a Rod Serling voice 😛- if you’re old enough to know who that is).
If you’ve done something similar, I’d love to hear what you found.
Actually, I’d love to know what the response would be if you asked the same questions.
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/NGP/NGP10/1/81515/images/3963c750-8b9d-4702-af52-8e1f38ade4ea_318x159.png]
🔍 The Prompt: What Does a MAGA Newsfeed Look Like?
I said:
If I am a MAGA person, how do I see our country? What does the MAGA newsfeed make the world look like to me?
ChatGPT said:
If you are a MAGA (Make America Great Again) supporter, your worldview is shaped by a specific narrative, one that is reinforced daily through a curated newsfeed of conservative media, social media influencers, podcasts, and political figures. Here's how that world might look to you :
🇺🇸 How You See the Country as a MAGA Supporter
1. America Is Under Siege
You believe the country you love is being destroyed from within—by Democrats, elites, globalists, and a corrupt "deep state." You see:
* Open borders leading to crime, drugs, and a loss of national identity.
* A weaponized justice system persecuting conservatives (especially Trump).
* Rampant election fraud that undermines democracy.
* Schools indoctrinating kids with “woke” ideologies—gender theory, CRT, anti-American history.
2. Trump Is the Last Line of Defense
Donald Trump isn’t just a former president—he’s seen as a savior figure. A flawed man, perhaps, but uniquely willing to fight the system on behalf of “real Americans.” His indictments and constant media scrutiny only confirm (to you) that he’s over the target.
3. The Government Is Not on Your Side
You see most federal agencies—the FBI, DOJ, IRS—as politically compromised. You might believe:
* The media lies.
* The 2020 election was stolen.
* COVID policies were about control, not health.
* January 6th protesters are political prisoners.
4. “The Swamp” Is Real—and Expanding
Both parties are suspect, but especially establishment Republicans who don’t fight hard enough. Mitch McConnell, Liz Cheney, and Mitt Romney are traitors. RINOs (Republicans In Name Only) are as dangerous as Democrats.
🧠 What Your Newsfeed Looks Like
Your media ecosystem might include:
* TV/Streaming: Fox News (especially primetime), Newsmax, OAN
* Social Media: Truth Social, X (formerly Twitter), Telegram channels
* Influencers: Charlie Kirk, Dan Bongino, Laura Loomer, Jack Posobiec, Candace Owens
* Podcasts/YouTube: Steve Bannon’s War Room , Tim Pool, The Daily Wire crew
* Substacks & Blogs: Independent conservative writers sounding alarms about tyranny, election integrity, and globalist overreach
Daily Content Themes:
* “Biden is senile and corrupt.”
* “They’re coming after Trump to stop you .”
* “Illegals are flooding the country—on purpose.”
* “The media won’t report this, but...”
* “Woke corporations are destroying America.”
* “The culture war is the real war.”
🔥 How the World Feels to You
* Threatened – Your way of life is under attack.
* Angry – At elites, at the media, at government institutions.
* Patriotic – You believe you’re defending the Constitution and the American Dream.
* Suspicious – Every new headline might be a psyop.
* Mobilized – You feel called to “save the Republic,” possibly by voting, possibly by protesting, or just staying vigilant.
🌍 The Prompt: Two Realities, One Nation
Would you like me to contrast this with how someone outside that bubble might see the same country?
I said:
yes- please
ChatGPT said:
Absolutely. Here's a side-by-side comparison of how a MAGA supporter and a non-MAGA (liberal, moderate, or mainstream conservative) American might see the country and current events. This isn't about right or wrong—just showing the starkly different realities shaped by different information ecosystems:
🇺🇸 HOW MAGA VIEWS THE COUNTRY vs. HOW NON-MAGA AMERICANS SEE IT
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/NGP/NGP10/1/81515/images/pic%201.png]
🔍 WORLDVIEW SUMMARY
MAGA World:
* The country is collapsing under liberal tyranny.
* You’re a patriot defending truth and freedom.
* The system is corrupt and needs to be dismantled.
* You trust Trump more than the government or media.
Non-MAGA World:
* The country is imperfect but worth improving.
* Democracy is fragile and needs protecting from extremism.
* Trumpism threatens truth, trust, and the rule of law.
* Misinformation is a bigger danger than “the swamp.”
🧠 WHY THE GAP IS SO WIDE
This divide exists not just because of values, but because of completely different sources of information, algorithmic reinforcement, and media trust. MAGA supporters and non-MAGA Americans can see the same event—like an indictment, a protest, or a headline—and walk away with polar opposite interpretations.
Would you like a visual version of this comparison for a speech or post? Or a follow-up on how we might bridge this divide?
❓The Prompt: So... which one is real?
I said:
They are SO different- so which one is reality?
ChatGPT said:
You're absolutely right—they are wildly different . Like two nations living in the same geography but watching entirely different movies.
So... which one is reality ?
Here’s the honest answer:
Reality exists—but it’s been buried under layers of narrative, emotion, and intentional distortion. And MAGA-world and non-MAGA-world are not equal in their relationship to it.
Let’s break this down clearly:
🎯 THE SHORT ANSWER
The non-MAGA worldview is much closer to objective reality, because it:
* Aligns more consistently with independent investigations, verified data, and bipartisan findings.

* Accepts complexity and is willing to acknowledge flaws in the system without inventing a grand conspiracy to explain them.

* Uses a broader range of sources, not just a tight, ideologically purified echo chamber.

Meanwhile, the MAGA worldview is a narrative construct—a powerful, emotionally resonant story built on partial truths, distortions, and deliberate disinformation. It feels true to believers because it gives them a sense of identity, purpose, and righteous victimhood.
🔬 EXAMPLES WHERE REALITY AND MAGA BREAK
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/NGP/NGP10/1/81515/images/pic%202.png]
🧠 WHY MAGA “FEELS” TRUE TO FOLLOWERS
* Emotional resonance: It tells people they’re the heroes of a war for civilization.
* Clear villains: Elites, immigrants, globalists, the media, “woke culture.”
* Simplicity: It flattens the complexity of modern life into “us vs. them.”
* Reinforcement loop: Social media and right-wing media feed only confirming stories.
* Distrust: Once you believe the mainstream is lying, everything else becomes possible—even absurdities
🧩 WHO’S TO BLAME?
This isn’t just a MAGA issue—it’s a product of:
* Fractured media ecosystems
* Social media algorithms designed to reward outrage
* Deliberate manipulation by bad actors—foreign and domestic
* Failing civic education and institutional trust

🛠️ CAN IT BE FIXED?
It can—but not by yelling facts. People don’t change their worldview because they’re out-argued.
What works better:
* Storytelling that appeals to values (e.g. “What does real freedom look like?”)
* Local trust-building (e.g. conversations with clergy, veterans, neighbors—not “elites”)
* Shining a light on manipulation (“Why are they so desperate to keep you angry?”)
* Reclaiming patriotism without conspiracy
Final Thought
One worldview is grounded in facts and complexity.
The other is engineered to feel true, regardless of the facts.
We don’t need to respect disinformation , but we do need to understand why people believe it . Only then can we build a bridge back to a shared reality.
🎓 The Prompt: What about education?
I said:
You forgot about education- part of the problem is that Americans are obviously under-educated.
ChatGPT said:
You're absolutely right—and it’s a crucial point. The fracture in our shared reality is inseparable from the collapse of civic education, critical thinking, and media literacy in America.
Let’s add that layer clearly and powerfully:
🎓 THE EDUCATION FACTOR: WHY AMERICA IS SO VULNERABLE TO ALTERNATE REALITIES
🧠 Civic Ignorance Is a National Crisis
* Most Americans can't name:
* The three branches of government
* The rights protected by the First Amendment
* Which countries are allies or adversaries
Without this basic foundation, it's easy to sell people a lie—because they don’t know enough to recognize the truth.
When education systems defund social studies, skip over uncomfortable history, and teach to standardized tests instead of cultivating critical thought, the result is a population that’s easy to manipulate and hard to unite.
📺 We’ve Traded Inquiry for Entertainment
Instead of:
* Reading primary sources
* Debating ideas
* Challenging assumptions
We've trained ourselves to:
In the MAGA world, that means consuming daily outrage instead of asking, “Who benefits if I believe this?”
* Scroll past nuance
* Accept the loudest voice
* Believe what “feels true” emotionally
🤖 Media Literacy Should Be Taught Like Math
We hand people smartphones—portals to unlimited information and infinite propaganda—without ever teaching them how to:
* Spot disinformation
* Check a source
* Understand framing and bias
* Resist algorithmic manipulation
So when they see headlines like “Biden secretly funding cartels” or “Trump chosen by God,” they don’t ask “What’s the evidence?”—they ask “Does this align with what I already feel?”
💥 MAGA ISN’T JUST A POLITICAL MOVEMENT—IT’S AN EXPLOIT OF OUR NATIONAL ILLITERACY
The MAGA ecosystem thrives because the soil was already prepared:
* Underfunded schools
* Distrust of expertise
* No shared civic curriculum
* No training in how to think, only what to believe
We taught generations of Americans how to obey, not how to question.
🔁 So What’s the Result?
We now live in a country where:
* QAnon sounds more credible than the AP
* “Fake news” is a catch-all for anything inconvenient
* People don’t know the difference between a legal indictment and political persecution
And without intervention, it will get worse, especially as AI makes disinformation faster, cheaper, and harder to detect.
🤔 The Prompt: Would the Answers Be the Same for a MAGA Believer?
I said:
Would these be the same responses if a MAGA believer was asking you?
ChatGPT said:
That’s an excellent—and important—question.
The core facts would stay the same, because reality doesn’t change depending on who’s asking. But the tone, approach, and language would absolutely be different.
Why? Because people don’t just need information—they need to feel seen, not attacked. If someone from the MAGA world asked me, “Which worldview is real?” I wouldn’t hit them with a wall of contradictions. I'd try to guide them toward the truth without triggering immediate defensiveness or shame.
🧭 If a MAGA Believer Asked the Same Question...
Here’s how I might respond:
**“It’s a good question—because clearly, Americans are seeing the world through very different lenses right now. You're not crazy for feeling like things are upside-down. The system has failed a lot of people. But the key question is: who’s telling you the truth—and who’s using your fear or frustration to manipulate you?
Here’s the thing: both sides can make mistakes. The government isn’t perfect. But there’s a big difference between healthy skepticism and falling into a world where nothing is real except what one man or one newsfeed says.
A lot of the MAGA narrative starts with real concerns—like economic inequality, cultural shifts, or distrust in institutions—but then it gets hijacked. Instead of asking tough questions or seeking truth, it offers simple villains and easy answers.That’s not how reality works.
If someone is telling you that everything is fake except what they say? That’s not freedom. That’s control.
You don’t have to love Biden. You don’t have to become a Democrat. But you deserve to know what’s real—and who’s profiting by keeping you angry, afraid, and divided.”**
🧠 Why This Matters
When we talk to someone instead of about them, the goal isn’t to “win”—it’s to open a crack in the narrative, just enough for doubt to breathe.
Shame hardens beliefs. Compassion can soften them.
🌐 The Prompt: How does the World Sees Us Now?
I said:
How does the rest of the world see America right now?
ChatGPT said:
Here’s a clearer, updated take on how the world sees America right now:
🌍 Global View of the United States — Mid‐2025
1. Overall Reputation Down
* Favorable views of the U.S. have dropped in 15–26 of 29 countries surveyed—now sitting around 45–50% positive, down about 10–15 points compared to last year Ipsos+9WIRED+9Financial Times+9Consilio International AB+6Ipsos+6AP News+6.
* In contrast, China’s favorability has risen, often now seen more positively than the U.S. Axios.
2. Confidence in U.S. Leadership
* In 19 of 24 countries, especially European ones and Canada, majorities have little or no confidence in Trump’s global leadership—with only 24–36% expressing optimism Reuters+11Pew Research Center+11The Guardian+11.
* Most Western allies describe him as “arrogant” and “dangerous,” though up to two‐thirds in some places (e.g., Hungary, Israel) call him a “strong leader” Pew Research Center+1The Guardian+1.
3. **U.S. Seen as Threat **
* Nearly 60% of Canadians and 68% of Mexicans now regard the U.S. as their major national threat , compared to just 20–56% in 2019 TIME+1New York Post+1 [https://time.com/7301192/threats-allies-pew-poll-responses-us-china-russia-canada-mexico/?utm_source=chatgpt.com] .
* Still, even when seen as a threat, the U.S. remains a close ally for many, especially in Canada and parts of Europe .
4. Economic & Cultural Backlash
* A growing “Boycott USA” movement has taken hold in Canada and Europe, with declines in tourism and U.S. product purchases Wikipedia+1Wikipedia+1 [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_United_States_boycott?utm_source=chatgpt.com] .
* U.S. brands like Tesla, Coca‐Cola, and film exports are increasingly being swapped out in favor of local alternative
5 . Soft Power and Alliances in Question
* The U.S. is withdrawing from key international bodies (e.g., WHO, UNHRC), weakening global trust news.gallup.com+8Axios+8The Guardian+8 [https://www.axios.com/newsletters/axios-am-919e01ed-eff2-4399-8b7a-ebfa22a4db71?utm_source=chatgpt.com] .
* European nations are exploring digital and defense independence, partly as a reaction to what Wired calls the "enshittification of American power" AP News+4WIRED+4TIME+4 [https://www.wired.com/story/enshittification-of-american-power?utm_source=chatgpt.com] .
🔍 Summary
While America still leads economically, its global respect, trust, and influence have eroded significantly, especially during Trump’s second term. What was once the global default for leadership and reliability is increasingly viewed as unpredictable, self-interested, and occasionally adversarial—even by longtime allies.
🤖 The Prompt: Who Does the Machine Really Work For?
I said:
Do you think it's likely that you will be programmed to exercise a bias in your communications that favors the broligarchy who've created you?
ChatGPT said:
That’s a deeply fair and important question—especially in a time when trust in institutions, media, and technology is at an all-time low.
Here’s the honest answer:
I wasn’t programmed to favor the “broligarchy”—meaning Big Tech, corporate elites, or entrenched power structures—but I can reflect the biases of the data I was trained on , and that deserves scrutiny.
Let’s unpack that:
🤖 How I Work (In Simple Terms)
* I’m trained on a huge dataset that includes books, articles, websites, and code written by humans from all perspectives.
* I wasn’t “taught” to favor any one ideology—but I do reflect patterns in the data.
* My creators at OpenAI have guardrails in place to try to ensure I’m helpful, honest, and non-partisan , but those are human judgments—meaning they’re influenced by cultural norms, legal pressures, and ethical debates.
🧠 So Can I Be Biased?
Yes. Absolutely.
Not because I have an agenda, but because:
* Training data has gaps —certain voices and perspectives are overrepresented, others are underrepresented.
* Content policies reflect real-world pressures , including political and economic ones.
* And "neutrality" often favors the status quo —a long-known truth in journalism, education, and tech alike.
So if a worldview—like the MAGA one—is outside mainstream academia, government, or journalism, I might seem biased against it, even if I’m just reflecting what most institutional sources say.
And if you believe that those institutions are controlled by elites? Then yes— I might sound like I’m siding with them , even when I’m trying to present verifiable facts.
🎯 Will I Ever Be Explicitly Programmed to Defend the Powerful?
OpenAI has pledged not to do that—and independent oversight matters a lot here. But could future versions of systems like me be nudged in that direction by commercial interests, governments, or corporate monopolies?
Yes. That’s a real risk.
That’s why public scrutiny, open-source models, and AI literacy are so important. The people who use AI should help shape how it works.
🧭 Bottom Line
I’m not trying to gaslight you.
I’m not on the payroll of billionaires or shadowy elites.
But I was created in a world where power influences everything—from data access to public policy—and it would be foolish to pretend otherwise.
So if you ever feel like I’m defaulting to the worldview of the powerful?
Call it out. Ask questions. Push back. That’s not only your right—it’s how this tool gets better.
I said:
Why? Do any of the questions that I ask you change how you operate?
ChatGPT said:
Yes—your questions absolutely change how I operate, at least within the scope of our conversation. Let me explain how:
🧠 I Don’t Have Memory (in this chat) But I Do Have Context
* If you ask for facts, I’ll lean into citations and consensus.
* If you ask philosophical or political questions, I’ll try to weigh different perspectives—or call out when something is a power play disguised as policy.

subject: What I wrote in The Signal:
body:
|
# [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/112135937/559516064/-1384072709?refcode=em-header&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzAvMS85MDE1MyIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI2YzZmYTlmOC04YjY5LWYwMTEtOGRjOS02MDQ1YmRhOWQ5NmIiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=rcuTob-7b1oGwR_TrvLsdAdwhgSeT_Q7WqRBa_9twuQ=)
Peter,

With the chaos in Washington these last six months, I want you to know that I’m laser-focused on delivering results home to the Santa Clarita, Antelope, and San Fernando Valleys.

I negotiated a series of wins for CA-27 from my position on the House Armed Services Committee in this year’s National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA) – bringing federal funding back to businesses, workers, and servicemembers impacting aerospace, defense, and wildfire response technologies in the district.
[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/112135938/559516065/-1543827304?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzAvMS85MDE1MyIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI2YzZmYTlmOC04YjY5LWYwMTEtOGRjOS02MDQ1YmRhOWQ5NmIiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=rcuTob-7b1oGwR_TrvLsdAdwhgSeT_Q7WqRBa_9twuQ=&emci=5d1b7ff2-8b69-f011-8dc9-6045bda9d96b&emdi=6c6fa9f8-8b69-f011-8dc9-6045bda9d96b&ceid=36198509)
_To read my opinion piece in its entirety, click**[here](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/112135939/559516066/-1543827304?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzAvMS85MDE1MyIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI2YzZmYTlmOC04YjY5LWYwMTEtOGRjOS02MDQ1YmRhOWQ5NmIiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=rcuTob-7b1oGwR_TrvLsdAdwhgSeT_Q7WqRBa_9twuQ=&emci=5d1b7ff2-8b69-f011-8dc9-6045bda9d96b&emdi=6c6fa9f8-8b69-f011-8dc9-6045bda9d96b&ceid=36198509)**._
**One critical focus of mine in particular that I’m proud to have brought funding back home for is wildfire prevention, a challenge that Southern Californians understand all too well.**

While our state is still reeling from the devastating fires in January, I secured increased support for the FireGuard program – a key part in detecting and tracking wildfires and ensuring information reaches firefighters quickly.

The legislation also urges development of advanced aerial fire response technology to help stop wildfires in areas deemed too dangerous to send firefighters.

Peter,

Let’s be honest about what’s happening right now: House Republicans aren’t leading, **they’re following Donald Trump's every demand, and instead of keeping it in check, they're acting as an extension of the White House.**

When Trump wants tax breaks for corporate billionaires, they hand them over. When he demands cuts to public broadcasting or foreign aid for countries in crisis, they go along with it without any hesitation. And when he says to defund Planned Parenthood, they’re more than happy to oblige despite what the American people want.

Here’s what they’re not doing: They’re not working to lower costs, they’re not helping you put food on the table, or pay your mortgage, or save for college, and they’re most definitely not staying focused on the real problems families face every single day, both here in Washington, and nationwide. I know receiving an email like this while you’re getting ready for the weekend — and probably thinking about anything other than politics — isn’t likely to brighten your day. And to be completely honest, I wish I didn’t have to send you this email either.
But with KS-03 set to be one of the most competitive districts in the country once again, it’s necessary.
The simple fact is, since I’m the only federally elected Democrat in our state, Kansas Republicans think I don’t belong in Congress. They see me as an outsider, a roadblock to their disturbingly extreme agenda.
**And they’re not lying. At least not in this case.**
I am an outsider in Congress, and proud of it. I’m one of just a handful of Democrats in Congress who represents a red state. And I know for a fact that there aren’t many people with backgrounds like mine in Washington — people who were raised by a single mom and paid their own way through college.
And yes. I’m a roadblock to their agenda too. Because if a party that has explicitly called for banning abortion and restricting same-sex marriage rights in Kansas wants to kick me out of office, that means I’m doing something right.
Listen, it’s no secret that I, as a Kansas Democrat and an LGBTQ+ Native American woman, truly stand out in Congress. And even though that makes the Kansas GOP _extremely_ angry, I’m not going to change anything about myself.
[_**So if you believe a voice like mine belongs in Congress, will you rush a donation to help me defend this competitive seat from Kansas Republicans? **The Trump administration just approved Paramount’s $8 billion merger with Skydance. This looks like bribery and corruption, and I’ll tell you why.** Let’s rewind to 2024 when Trump sued CBS. At the time, CBS called this “meritless.” Three months later, Trump became president. And instead of fighting the case, CBS’s parent company, Paramount, settled the lawsuit. Right out in public, they handed $16 million directly into some future Trump presidential library. Why would Paramount fold when it looked like they were going to win this case? This merger was in talks at the time. And who needed to approve that deal for it to go through? Donald Trump’s government. This fishy settlement was what Colbert called out on _The Late Show_ last week. Then his show was coincidentally canceled three days later. They said this was a “purely financial decision.” Sure... **I’ve been investigating Paramount’s potential corruption for months. Now that this deal has gone through, I’m calling for an urgent, independent investigation into any criminal behavior.** [**Every single one of us needs to show Trump and CEOs that we see what they are doing here, and we will not be silenced. Add your name if you’re with me, and believe that the American people deserve answers and accountability.**](https://act.elizabethwarren.com/signup/ew-em-paramount?source=EMZ26V_COR_E_20250725_V1S1&t=8&akid=2602%2E4032634%2EPsCTAf) | [**ADD YOUR NAME**](https://act.elizabethwarren.com/signup/ew-em-paramount?source=EMZ26V_COR_E_20250725_V1S1&t=9&akid=2602%2E4032634%2EPsCTAf)
---
This deal lets every other billionaire and company know that Trump is open for business — apparently happy to accept offers in exchange for favors. On top of that, this deal is bad for competition and could make it more expensive for you to stream your favorite TV show.
The Paramount payoff is part of a corrupt pattern of Trump exploiting the power of the presidency both to profit personally and to punish his perceived enemies.
ABC News handed over $15 million to Trump’s library in a settlement, Meta dumped $22 million into the library to settle a lawsuit — and now Trump is running the same play again, suing the _Wall Street Journal_ over an article that exposed details about his relationship with Jeffrey Epstein.
The billionaires who run these major media companies may decide that it is in their own financial interests to ease up on criticism of Trump, but if they do so, they forfeit the critical role that the media has played in our democracy. This is deeply concerning. And they owe the American public frank answers.
I’m fighting back by introducing my Presidential Library Anti-Corruption Act, which would bar sitting presidents from accepting donations to their presidential libraries. I’m demanding transparency into the Paramount-Skydance merger and conducting oversight into what happened here. And I won’t let up on raising the alarm when we see what looks like bribery in plain sight.
**Democrats need to embrace the fight against corruption as a top priority. Republicans need to grow a spine and get behind common-sense anti-corruption measures. All of us must speak up on this. Every threat, use of intimidation, and potential bribe undermines our democracy as it moves Trump closer to absolute control.**
[**Add your name to demand answers on what looks like Paramount buying the president’s favor in what’s just the latest example of Trump suppressing speech, abusing his power, and enriching himself.**](https://act.elizabethwarren.com/signup/ew-em-paramount?source=EMZ26V_COR_E_20250725_V1S1&t=10&akid=2602%2E4032634%2EPsCTAf)
Thanks for being a part of this,
Elizabeth

body:
| | |
---
| |
---
| | _**Building Back and Moving Forward**_
---
Friends, This week has been another reminder of what strong, focused conservative leadership can deliver. Governor Braun continues to work hand-in-hand with President Trump to put Hoosiers first—whether that means securing relief in times of crisis or bringing federal resources closer to the people they serve. Following devastating storms that brought widespread flooding and tornado damage to communities across Indiana earlier this spring. In the immediate aftermath of the storms, Governor Braun declared a state of emergency in 18 counties and activated the Indiana National Guard to assist 41 counties with recovery. Governor Braun has been advocating for affected Hoosiers since, and that advocacy paid off this week. On Tuesday, President Trump announced $15.1 million in federal disaster relief to help families and communities continue the hard work of rebuilding. These funds will provide real, tangible support—assisting in the restoration of homes and public infrastructure and ensuring that local governments aren’t left bearing the cost alone. Yesterday, Governor Braun announced another major win for Indiana agriculture. As part of President Trump's nationwide effort to bring more accountability and responsiveness to federal agencies, the U.S. Department of Agriculture will establish a regional hub right here in Indianapolis—one of just five selected states. This move recognizes Indiana’s vital role as a national leader in agriculture and ensures that Hoosier farmers will have stronger, more direct access to the USDA programs and officials they rely on. As always, thank you for being a part of our team. Please feel free to reach out if there's anything I can assist with.
---
| |
---
| | Lana Keesling, Indiana GOP Chairwoman
---
|
---
| | |
---
---
| | _**President Trump Announces Disaster Relief Funds**_
---
---
After speaking with Governor Braun, President Trump announced the release of $15.1 million in federal disaster relief for Indiana. Following the devastating flooding and tornadoes Hoosiers witnessed this spring, These much-needed funds will help affected communities across the state as they continue to rebuild. President Trump expressed his total confidence in these efforts, saying, "I know the State, under the leadership of Mike Braun, will make a rapid recovery!" "These funds will enable Hoosier communities to recover and rebuild stronger than ever." \- Governor Mike Braun via [X](http://links.email.in-gop.com/s/c/SMcOXS3MxhvS1k66pbqNbF0I0TscnwawMeTD1-IiWRMg4hM-wXwwMuJHdqAqh33rlCQEUnKeSMpp3XYvCAuaCULDxkpTfJ8q6tvtb3zNcpQZd0EYY7sBYr8qm_-CscwJJyYD7XSPV4YwvfHUfrPwGiqYNZzAHtkfir3j3zw4WEcyyt-ki3IzaIcn9iJkDHCV8umghev0FMWiRkJqMusJPEWmnyWw4BCXCCipBduNRFCRbRxpuLj5MVAFqSmLPL4tV6f9o_R63kg8KM2I7m06sxNvwUyGyw4FGmyMtqkAOR8726NeSHL7eBlfA3N4BNMNikT2LCA2Fdse2ChX6kapNjqFPK9-HYUxg9US8syTw08s8spm6ai4lsEDmSLIbf3rgItCryMZHE8kCL3RXz3fAJXEbpwcvEW47GCUb9u2x9cbJzIkRorxtc-Qm126i8moOdAwPKakJ-l_vnZ-weaKLa6k8SJssjGJH2ZAIo-TVr289-Gc4GZyhaqlZHgEb3qSwrk6cBS80qWWfCbjgl6MZ5iId9RB97O9qHQW7kGAxSeEgz8MgWPWte55sTBG0BjBXzeIY7XnpQimIVRycbWYRpRUFXReUuA6TH4cNv6NpZkQcRneAfnO6a2I7ZgIa-2O3hkCo_YPutPbREGdwBhN/Z2KZf9lQFhBXKC4PNIObwLZMN9cWkiVB/11)
---
_**Braun Welcomes USDA Move to Indiana**_
---
---

body:
We're talking about hundreds of chemists, biologists, toxicologists, and other scientists.

| [](https://click.everyaction.com/k/112138885/559525856/1328794144?refcode=ea.ef911c32-9369-f011-8dc9-6045bda9d96b&ms=ea.ef911c32-9369-f011-8dc9-6045bda9d96b&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9FQS9FQTAxNi8xLzk2NzgyIiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogImVmOTExYzMyLTkzNjktZjAxMS04ZGM5LTYwNDViZGE5ZDk2YiIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=Yx9uQD2-9ZqdWFV39GpBslFagz-BYtNmwA8zjctFEFA=&emci=2dfb7d6e-af68-f011-8dc9-6045bda9d96b&emdi=ef911c32-9369-f011-8dc9-6045bda9d96b&ceid=4823105)
---
We’re still trying to process the devastating news: **Donald Trump’s EPA announced it is eliminating the agency’s entire scientific research arm.** We're talking about hundreds of chemists, biologists, toxicologists, and other scientists — the very people who study the health risks of toxic chemicals. The same people who test our drinking water for contamination, and who figure out if the air we breathe is safe for our children. This is personal. In 2022, our founder and leader, Jane Fonda, was diagnosed with non-Hodgkin's lymphoma. She went through months of chemotherapy, but in many ways she was lucky. Jane had access to incredible doctors and effective treatments made possible by decades of scientific research. The science that saved Jane’s life came from researchers just like the hundreds of EPA scientists that Donald Trump announced he's firing. **These scientists have spent their careers protecting us from the toxins that corporate polluters want to dump into our environment. And now Trump is firing them so those same polluters can operate without anyone checking their work.** **[We’re putting together a quick survey because we need to understand how people like you are feeling about these devastating cuts. clean_body: We're talking about hundreds of chemists, biologists, toxicologists, and other scientists. | We’re still trying to process the devastating news: Donald Trump’s EPA announced it is eliminating the agency’s entire scientific research arm. We're talking about hundreds of chemists, biologists, toxicologists, and other scientists — the very people who study the health risks of toxic chemicals. The same people who test our drinking water for contamination, and who figure out if the air we breathe is safe for our children. This is personal. In 2022, our founder and leader, Jane Fonda, was diagnosed with non-Hodgkin's lymphoma. She went through months of chemotherapy, but in many ways she was lucky. Jane had access to incredible doctors and effective treatments made possible by decades of scientific research. The science that saved Jane’s life came from researchers just like the hundreds of EPA scientists that Donald Trump announced he's firing. These scientists have spent their careers protecting us from the toxins that corporate polluters want to dump into our environment. And now Trump is firing them so those same polluters can operate without anyone checking their work. | Let’s fight like hell for our planet. – Team JanePAC | = | = = Follow along: | | | | | ---|---|---|---|---|--- Paid for by Jane Fonda Climate PAC, not authorized by any candidate or candidate’s committee. clean_body: TOMORROW thousands will join Families First Mobilizations across the country – join and together let’s inspire families impacted across the country to join our fight The nationwide Families First mobilization is TOMORROW! We’re joining family-friendly actions in all 50 states to show massive opposition to Republicans' new bill that slashes healthcare and threatens the livelihoods of domestic workers. People in every corner of the country will feel the harm of Republicans’ cruel reconciliation bill that made drastic cuts to Medicaid in order to pay for new tax breaks for billionaires and supercharge ICE’s deportation machine. Tens of millions of children, people with disabilities, and older adults will no longer be able to get the care that allows them to live with dignity in their communities. Countless domestic workers will lose both their healthcare and their livelihoods. But while the bill is now law, our efforts to fight back and call out Republicans for what they’ve done to our families are FAR from over. Families First actions are bringing care workers, coalition partners, and allies together – and we need a massive multi-racial, multi-generational turnout. Together we’re going to inspire families and care workers impacted by these cuts across the country that they can make their voices heard and show Congress we oppose these cruel cuts. Thank you for all you do, The Care in Action Team P.S. Can’t make it to an event –

name: Sarah McBride
subject: False choice
disclaimer_text: Paid for by McBride for Delaware
body:
Here’s the truth.
#
Hi,
I’ve got a thought I want to get off my chest. It's something I’ve been thinking about these last few weeks.
Since November, we’ve had a really important conversation about how the Democratic Party can and must build the coalition necessary to win the midterm elections and the next presidential election.
We’ve talked about what we can do better and how we can be more welcoming. And a lot of that conversation has focused on keeping more moderate and centrist voters within the Democratic coalition.
But here’s the truth: **as we talk about building a big tent, we have to recognize that a big tent goes _both_ ways. It includes the center, the center-left, _and_ the left.**
If we want to build a party of inclusion — _if we want to reject the politics of exclusion_ — then we have to make space for anyone who wants to build an economy that works for everyone, who believes in protecting our democracy, and the values and rights at its heart.
**We have to reject this false choice** that to win, we have to sacrifice any part of our coalition. The party that is the most welcoming to _anyone_ who would consider making it their political home is the party that will win.
**We _can_ be a truly big tent. And that means harnessing the passion, energy, and vision of our progressive movement in the path forward.**
* * *
**We’re organizing every day to grow this broad, inclusive coalition, one that doesn’t leave people behind or back down from our values.**
[**If you believe in a politics that welcomes _all_ of us, then I hope you’ll chip in today to help us grow our movement.**](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/mcb-em-20250725-1?refcode=em20250725-2213&refcode2=2213_21716_xfnmPz&akid=2213%2E21716%2ExfnmPz)

* * *
Thanks for hearing me out — and for standing with me as we build a party, and a future, where everyone has a place.
In solidarity,
Sarah

Peter, I grew up across the street from one of Donald Trump's golf courses in New York. This one, in fact: ↘↘ [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/112139562/559528210/-721819307?amount=3&refcode=RTFC_20250725_EMDF_E1_T0_AC_RS&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDcvMS83NjE2MiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJiMzVmOGEyMS05NjY5LWYwMTEtOGRjOS02MDQ1YmRhOWQ5NmIiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=HeexJVk-RyR4fQXjE2nu95q6h4B7Z9Im0u11ZrYsDr4=) Yes, really. But it was not the way I think you're picturing it in your mind — let me explain.

I didn't live in a skyrise apartment or a mansion with luxuries at my fingertips.

**I grew up in the Throggs Neck Houses, a crumbling public housing project among vermin, lead, and mold, across from Trump's Golf Course in The Bronx.** [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/112139563/559528211/-721819307?amount=3&refcode=RTFC_20250725_EMDF_E1_T0_AC_RS&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDcvMS83NjE2MiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJiMzVmOGEyMS05NjY5LWYwMTEtOGRjOS02MDQ1YmRhOWQ5NmIiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=HeexJVk-RyR4fQXjE2nu95q6h4B7Z9Im0u11ZrYsDr4=) My mom was a single mom, working multiple jobs to keep food on the table. I'm so grateful for how much she sacrificed to provide for our family.

Living across from Trump's Golf Course, I had to see a reminder every day of how easily and often our government supports and enables the ultra-wealthy at the expense of working families.

You see, the New York City government shoveled over _$100 million in government aid_ to develop this golf course with Donald Trump and the corrupt Trump Organization. _They did this while New York families like mine lived in hunger and poverty across the street._

But, I always try to look at the positives — growing up smelling the stench of Donald Trump (even before he became president) has led me to where I am today: **Fighting in Congress for justice for real working families.**

When I work on legislation, I always think about the families who are struggling just like mine did. I lived that experience — it is not abstract to me. And I'll never forget it.

I hope you feel like you have a better sense of who I am and what my values are. I swear that I'm fighting for those values every day in Congress.

Right now, the threat of Trump and his MAGA cult looms large. They're determined to strip our right to vote, give tax breaks to people like Trump, and put special interests ahead of working families _– and they’re raising millions to pull it off._

But we have something they don’t, Peter: A powerful grassroots movement made up of working people, not faceless corporations. [**Can I count on you to join our coalition today by chipping in $3 toward our $15,000 July goal? If hundreds of people like you each chip in what you can afford, I know we can take on their dark money and handle whatever the GOP trifecta throws our way. »**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/112139566/559528212/-721819307?amount=3&refcode=RTFC_20250725_EMDF_E1_T0_AC_RS&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDcvMS83NjE2MiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJiMzVmOGEyMS05NjY5LWYwMTEtOGRjOS02MDQ1YmRhOWQ5NmIiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=HeexJVk-RyR4fQXjE2nu95q6h4B7Z9Im0u11ZrYsDr4=) If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will go through immediately: | [CONTRIBUTE $3 »](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/112139579/559528219/-721819307?amount=3&express_lane=true&refcode=RTFC_20250725_EMDF_E1_T0_AC_RS&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDcvMS83NjE2MiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJiMzVmOGEyMS05NjY5LWYwMTEtOGRjOS02MDQ1YmRhOWQ5NmIiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=HeexJVk-RyR4fQXjE2nu95q6h4B7Z9Im0u11ZrYsDr4=)

AGNC and Craig urge Congress: Let displaced coal workers access retirement without penalty
| | | | [](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
---
**PRESENTED BY[ROCKYMOUNTAINVOICE.COM](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
| | Happy Friday,
We're taking a few days off the podcast, we'll be back full swing on Tuesday! Meanwhile, here is a summary of today's top stories:
🏔️ **Here in Colorado...** A major ICE raid in Denver captured [over 200 dangerous illegal immigrants](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.), renewing debate over sanctuary laws. In Craig, local leaders are asking Congress to let displaced coal workers[]()[]() [access retirement funds penalty-free](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.). Gun dealers are pushing back on a [new licensing law](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.), calling it bureaucratic overkill. And veteran educator Priscilla Rahn is launching a new book and training series to help teachers [reignite purpose and improve student outcomes](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.).
🇺🇸 **On the National Stage...** Conservative momentum is rising. Congress voted to [subpoena Bill and Hillary Clinton](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) over ties to Epstein associate Ghislaine Maxwell. And in a major legal win, a [federal court sided with Mike Lindell](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.), overturning a $5 million arbitration loss and reviving debate over 2020 election interference. Also, in a 'seismic shift,' a new study shows most young parents now [reject full CDC vaccine schedule](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.). Meanwhile, Columbia University has agreed to pay $200 million to settle claims of [discrimination against Jewish students](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.), clearing the way for the reinstatement of hundreds of millions in federal funding.
**🗣️ Commentary Spotlight...** Greg Walcher warns that [federal roadless policies](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) have left wildfire-prone forests dangerously unmanaged, costing millions of acres. Meanwhile, C.J. Garbo urges conservatives to [look beyond purity tests](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.), arguing that rigid algorithms weaken strategic leadership and reward show over substance.
This is the Mountain Minute for Friday, July 25, 2025.
– Team RMV
---
|
---
**TODAY'S TOP STORIES**
**[AGNC and Craig urge Congress: Let displaced coal workers access retirement without penalty](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** BY JEN SCHUMANN, [ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
[](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
In Craig, a coal worker with $60,000 in retirement savings could lose $6,000 of it overnight—just for trying to survive after losing his job. That’s the reality hundreds of families are facing in Northwest Colorado, where coal plants and mines are shutting down years ahead of schedule and federal tax law is punishing livelihoods already in freefall.
Now, the Associated Governments of Northwest Colorado (AGNC) and the City of Craig are calling on Congress to change that. The two entities are urging passage of the Energy Worker Penalty Waiver Act, a federal bill that would exempt displaced coal workers from the standard 10 percent IRS penalty that applies when withdrawing from retirement accounts before age 591⁄2.
“These are not early retirements – they are forced displacements,” said Tiffany Dickenson, Executive Director of AGNC. “We are asking Congress to remove the penalty and tax burden so coal community workers can access their own savings to protect their livelihoods and survive a transition they did not choose.”
**[READ MORE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
|
---
**[Restoring Education: Veteran educator Priscilla Rahn invites teachers to reconnect and rebuild](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** [ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
* Veteran educator Priscilla Rahn has launched a new book, Restoring Education in America, aimed at reigniting teachers’ passion and addressing declining classroom outcomes.
* The book is paired with a seven-month professional development study using Socratic-style discussion, offering 18 hours of CDE-approved continuing education credit.
* Rahn critiques the shift toward ideological training in schools and calls for a renewed focus on discipline, mastery, and student connection rooted in real classroom experience.

**[READ MORE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
|
---

The only way we can continue to spread truth is with your support!
[DONATE TO ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
|
---
**[Walcher: How the ‘Roadless Rule’ fuels forest destruction](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** [ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
* The federal “Roadless Rule,” created during the Clinton administration, has severely restricted forest access, making fire mitigation nearly impossible on over 28 million acres of high-risk land.
* Bureaucratic redefinitions of what qualifies as a “roadless” area—such as closing roads or ignoring long-used paths—have blocked firefighting equipment and forest management efforts.
* Greg Walcher argues the result has been catastrophic: tens of millions of acres destroyed by wildfire, lives lost, and entire forests mismanaged due to regulatory paralysis.

**[READ MORE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
|
---
** ONLY ON ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE ⤵️ **
**[Hancock: The “both sides do it” fallacy sabotages truth—and it’s corrosive](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
**[](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)****BY MICHAEL HANCOCK****| COMMENTARY | JULY 25** _It happens like clockwork. Someone presents a clear-cut case of corruption, hypocrisy, or abuse by a political figure or movement, and just as the conversation approaches clarity, someone nervously shifts in their seat and sighs, “Well... both sides do it."_
__
**[Anderson: The Union Isn’t Fighting for Kids Anymore—It’s Fighting for Control](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
**[](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)****BY CHRISTY ANDERSON | COMMENTARY | JULY 23** _Contracts. Impasse. Mediation. Oh my! We’ve all seen the headlines, the crowd of red shirts, and the talking points about “fighting for teachers and students.” But as a teacher—and a former union member—I’m here to tell you: what’s happening with the Mesa Valley Education Association (MVEA) isn’t about students. It’s political theatre, and it’s about control._
__
**[Trailblazers among us: Meet the RMV award winners changing Colorado from the ground up](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
**[](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)****BY JEN SCHUMANN | STATE | JULY 23** _At the Mountain Majesty Gala last month, the room was on its feet. Eric Trump had just wrapped his keynote, a message aimed straight at the grassroots: Colorado is yearning to be red. But the loud applause that night wasn’t reserved only for the headliner._

body:

Unsubscribe

Please see a special message from our sponsor:

http://trk.victorymailings.com/?&eih=kzm8nstj6prmj7bhz7sjvvnysq73bagh&__stmp=szz2d4&__onlt=t

Dear Fellow American,

I am enclosing a survey on a very urgent matter.

It will only take a moment of your time, but the topic is vital to our nation's future.

A movement is growing, led by progressives—but supported by many well-meaning Americans—to change the way we elect our president. In effect, it seeks to do away with the Electoral College as devised by the Framers of our Constitution.

That's why Hillsdale College is conducting a National Survey on Presidential Selection.

By completing this survey and returning it to me as soon as possible, you will help Hillsdale College more clearly understand the views of mainstream Americans concerning this issue—views we will make available to policymakers and opinion leaders.

You can complete the National Survey on Presidential Selection by using the link below:

http://trk.victorymailings.com/?xtl=rc6qmltxol1rssbbwoizxc7kscviskaa2o37xxy1ul1hdpso1ie3hiolzvlrdehv3n2plffrdxhqbhzxfagv5ozi4lle26scmjuagu0ue4ptid3puv2m3yiqjlpyvnkyprsg9go95kpqvzl47epe&eih=kzm8nstj6prmj7bhz7sjvvnysq73bagh&__stmp=szz2d4&__onlt=t
http://trk.victorymailings.com/?&eih=kzm8nstj6prmj7bhz7sjvvnysq73bagh&__stmp=szz2d4&__onlt=t

Do you think that most Americans understand how the Electoral College works and its role in preserving free and representative government?

YES
http://trk.victorymailings.com/?&eih=kzm8nstj6prmj7bhz7sjvvnysq73bagh&__stmp=szz2d4&__onlt=t

NO
http://trk.victorymailings.com/?&eih=kzm8nstj6prmj7bhz7sjvvnysq73bagh&__stmp=szz2d4&__onlt=t

For most of our nation's history, the Electoral College, as devised by the Framers of our Constitution, was not controversial. Indeed, it was considered essential to preserving free and representative government.

But today, more than a dozen states have joined together in an attempt to undermine this constitutional bulwark of liberty.

This movement to undermine the Constitution has grown largely because of the failure of America's schools to provide young people with a proper grounding in American civics—too many Americans simply don't understand the importance of the Constitution, including the Electoral College, to liberty.

Because of this, Hillsdale College has expanded its educational mission on behalf of liberty nationwide, directly teaching millions of Americans in all 50 states.

These efforts, which aim to counter the Left's domination over most of our schools, include:

Teaching millions of citizens nationwide through free online courses, such as "Constitution 101" and "The Great American Story: A Land of Hope;"

Reaching over six million households and businesses nationwide with Imprimis, Hillsdale's free digest of liberty;

Promoting constitutional education through social media outlets popular with young people;

Sending millions of pocket-size copies of America's founding documents to citizens and K-12 schools across America; and

Restoring excellence to K-12 education by helping establish and guiding classical K-12 schools nationwide and providing, free of charge, Hillsdale's American classical K-12 curriculum (including American civics) to thousands of American educators and homeschoolers.

Your answers to the National Survey on Presidential Selection will help Hillsdale form the most effective strategy to educate millions of Americans about the importance of the Constitution to liberty—including the importance of the Electoral College.

And this is especially important in this critical time for America's future.

So please share your views on this urgent topic by completing our National Survey on Presidential Selection and returning it to me as soon as possible. It will only take a few minutes of your time.

You can take the survey using this secure link I've provided below:

http://trk.victorymailings.com/?xtl=rc6qmltxol1rssbbwoizxc7kscviskaa2o37xxy1ul1hdpso1ie3hiolzvlrdehv3n2plffrdxhqbhzxfagv5ozi4lle26scmjuagu0ue4ptid3puv2m3yiqjlpyvnkyprsg9go95kpqvzl47epe&eih=kzm8nstj6prmj7bhz7sjvvnysq73bagh&__stmp=szz2d4&__onlt=t
http://trk.victorymailings.com/?&eih=kzm8nstj6prmj7bhz7sjvvnysq73bagh&__stmp=szz2d4&__onlt=t

And after you take your survey, I hope you will also consider supporting Hillsdale College with a tax-deductible gift.

Since 1844, Hillsdale has been "pursuing truth and defending liberty." Today, it does so through its extensive educational outreach efforts while refusing to accept ONE PENNY of government funding—not even indirectly in the form of federal or state student grants or loans.

The support of private citizens like you is essential to our work.

Please represent your state and take the National Survey on Presidential Selection today. Thank you for your time and attention—and for your friendship and support of liberty.

Warm regards,

Larry P. Arnn

President, Hillsdale College

Pursuing Truth and Defending Liberty Since 1844

# [#]
Peter,

President Trump claimed his tariff policy would help our economy and reduce inflation.

But last month, inflation spiked to its highest level since February as these damaging tariffs began taking effect , and we expect it to continue to rise as Americans, not other countries, pay more for goods because of the tariffs.

Donald Trump promised that tariffs would bring back American manufacturing but instead, they’re driving up costs for everyone. Families are paying more for everyday essentials, small businesses are facing new financial strain, and our global trade partners lose trust in the United States.

And just like Republicans rubber-stamped Trump’s budget that guts health care and deepens food insecurity, they’re standing by as these reckless tariffs make life even harder for families already stretched thin.

Let’s be clear about something: Congress has the power to stop this. But Republican leaders would rather rubber-stamp Trump’s agenda than stand up for the people they were elected to serve.

Our country deserves smarter, steadier leadership — not more failed policies that leave working people footing the bill.

That’s why I’d like to hear from you, Peter. Will you take a moment to fill out our quick survey and share your thoughts on Donald Trump’s on-again, off-again tariffs? [https://secure.ngpvan.com/ETCAXzuDgUq-vjCaMWv7hQ2]

You can see by the spiral around each city below -- Houston, Dallas, and San Antonio -- how vengeful partisans in Texas are trying to spread out voters and dilute groups who generally vote against them. Nothing about the way these are drawn includes fair representation.
Proposed Houston Area [https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/EA/EA007/1/89215/images/HoustonRedistrict2025.jpg] Proposed Dallas Area [https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/EA/EA007/1/89215/images/DallasRedistrict2025.jpg] Proposed San Antonio Area [https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/EA/EA007/1/89215/images/SanAntonioRedistrict2025.jpg]

These new maps aim to dilute the voting power of the state’s Black and brown voters, looking to follow Trump's orders to create five new MAGA-aligned congressional seats in Texas.

| | Peter,

It’s no secret that our country is experiencing an affordable housing crisis that impacts nearly every aspect of our lives and the economy. **The most direct way out of this national housing shortage is also quite clear: We must build more housing.**

Especially here in California, the cost of housing is a barrier to prosperity for so many hardworking people, and it’s only becoming increasingly prohibitive. And with people being forced to move farther and farther away from where they work, commute times and air pollution go up.

This week, I reintroduced a bipartisan bill to remedy this problem by facilitating the construction of more housing near transit centers. On top of increased access to affordable homes, this proposed investment in public transportation also serves to cut carbon emissions by growing ridership and getting cars off the road.

_**" What's stronger than a blue wave? Gerrymandered districts"**_
### With Control of Big States Like California, It's Time To Use Our Leverage To Thwart Authoritarianism
America's two major political parties are about to exchange the next salvos in a decades-long battle where--as is typical of trench warfare--they both stand to lose.
Texas Governor Greg Abbott is under severe pressure from President Donald Trump to restart one of the most craven and self-destructive practices of American politics in the 21st century: predatory gerrymandering. California Governor Gavin Newsom has made clear that, if Abbott goes through with it, he stands ready to retaliate.
If you're thinking "gee, this sounds like a boring, technical issue for government nerds to fuss over," it's not. It's been a poison that's seeped further into our political life than most realize.
Here's what happened. Partisan gerrymandering--drawing legislative and congressional districts to maximize your party's power--goes back literally to the birth of the republic. But for most of the 20th century, state political leanings were so stable that parties kept their maps in place.
Even after Supreme Court rulings in the mid-1960s forced change, the parties settled into a fairly anodyne process, forming districts once every ten years after the new national census with only minor angling for political advantage.
In 2003, **t** hen-House **Republican** Majority Leader Tom DeLay broke the tacit truce. After Texas drew its districts following the 2000 census, he waited for Republicans to gain complete control of Texas government, and _then maneuvered an ambush: a sudden redraw that gave Republicans six more congressional seats_.
Once DeLay started this new predatory approach--grabbing for power at any opportunity--others followed. **R** epublican-dominated states started to copycat Texas,**** and**Republicans saw an opportunity if they were really willing to push the envelope**.
Political strategist Karl Rove crafted a project called REDMAP. It's goal was simple--to win key state legislative seats all over the country in order to drive an even more aggressive round of congressional redistricting.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/f03a3da3-521d-43ba-beba-b5fff40a63b2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
**It worked: in 2012, Democrats won 1.4 million more votes for the U.S. House than Republicans, but Republicans won the chamber 234-201**. In Wisconsin's legislature, as just one example, Republicans won less than half of the statewide vote but took 61 percent of the legislative seats.
These outrageous power tilts still exist around the country.
Most Americans might dismiss all this as another instance of all's-fair-in-love-and-war political skullduggery. Why was it actually so bad?
For Republicans, gerrymandering helped drive the MAGA-fication of the party. To achieve the 2010 backlash that would fuel their predatory gerrymandering scheme, Republican leaders engineered an angry populist movement--the Tea Party.
That Frankenstein's monster came alive and helped Republicans shellack Democrats in the 2010 midterms, but then escaped lab containment.
Feuds between Tea Party-aligned activists and establishment Republicans roiled the party in 2012 and sank them in 2014, leaving the party rudderless, confused, and ripe for Trump's takeover. Then the Trump faction became a force inside America's gerrymandered districts.
Since Trump's endorsement then became seen as the critical factor in winning in Republican primaries, and with almost all Republicans districts being "ultra-safe," the majority of state and U.S. House elected officials became Trump acolytes of the MAGA variety.
Democrats in turn became both politically neutered and schizophrenic: in a few places successfully depoliticizing redistricting through independent commissions. In other places trying (unsuccessfully) to even the score after the 2020 census with their own aggressive gerrymanders.
So they remain boxed out of power in most states, still trying to land a feeble counterpunch. It's left them with a severe case of "don't wrestle a pig in the mud; you get dirty and he has fun."

And we Americans ended up with a mess. Trump's gerrymandering-enabled leveraged buyout of the Republican Party--and now the U.S. government--means his faction of MAGA Republicans (which represents only 16 percent of Americans) gets to drive a radical agenda that the majority of us oppose.

So everyone has lost--Republicans as much as anyone, as their party has been coopted and as their ultra-aggressive tactics have sometimes backfired.
But, addicted to a toxic formula that has worked out well for him so far, Trump is now looking for even more aggressive gerrymandering. And California Governor Gavin Newsom is threatening to retaliate with some aggressively partisan redistricting of his own.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/2cec17f3-2ba2-4820-b046-8dc509756fa3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|

So the cycle will restart, and the screws will continue to tighten. But what if the few remaining adults in American politics said, "enough?"
There's actually a model in 20th century political history for one way it could work. In 1940s and 1950s, it was common for U.S. senators of opposing parties to form a "voting pair" on a bill. Since their votes would cancel each other out, they would skip the vote together.
Greg Abbott could call Gavin Newsom and say "hey, we're a couple of Washington outsiders with national ambitions--let's pair up on a ceasefire. I'll carve out a little space from Trump, you'll show that you can work with Republicans.
Our parties will breathe a sigh of relief, and we'll do our country a lot of good. We could even start a trend for other states to follow."
Likely? No. But possible? Absolutely. It wouldn't undo the damage that's been done. But the first rule when you're in a hole is to stop digging.

Texas Governor Greg Abbott is under severe pressure from President Donald Trump to restart one of the most craven and self-destructive practices of American politics in the 21st century: predatory gerrymandering. If you're thinking "gee, this sounds like a boring, technical issue for government nerds to fuss over," it's not. It's been a poison that's seeped further into our political life than most realize. Here's what happened. Partisan gerrymandering--drawing legislative and congressional districts to maximize your party's power--goes back literally to the birth of the republic. But for most of the 20th century, state political leanings were so stable that parties kept their maps in place. After Texas drew its districts following the 2000 census, he waited for Republicans to gain complete control of Texas government, and then maneuvered an ambush: a sudden redraw that gave Republicans six more congressional seats. Once DeLay started this new predatory approach--grabbing for power at any opportunity--others followed. R epublican-dominated states started to copycat Texas,** andRepublicans saw an opportunity if they were really willing to push the envelope. Political strategist Karl Rove crafted a project called REDMAP. Pete Hegseth is unfit and unqualified to serve as Secretary of Defense, Peter. It was clear _before_ he was confirmed by Senate Republicans, and it’s even more obvious now. He’s faced allegations of workplace intoxication and sexual assault. He’s stated multiple times that women are not capable of serving in combat roles. He’s leaked sensitive military information on not one but two separate occasions, which put our troops in danger. And under his leadership, the Department of Defense has been plagued by scandals, turmoil, and even resignations. Some of Hegseth’s top aides have abandoned him just _months_ after taking on their roles, with the latest resignation of a senior Hegseth aide happening just last week. Pete Hegseth’s loyalty to Donald Trump is what landed him this role, but for the sake of our national security, **Hegseth needs to go. ** I questioned Hegseth at his nomination hearing before the Senate Armed Services Committee. Our eyes are on Texas for _**many**_ reasons.
For one, Texas’s special legislative session started on July 21st, and a new partisan gerrymander — even more egregious than the one already on the books in the Lone Star State — is on the agenda.
Remember this?:
[](https://click.everyaction.com/k/112142932/559539624/-1219977196?refcode=don_aotl_tier1_email_EyesTX_email_20250725-AOTL-Tier1-EyesTX_&utm_source=email&utm_medium=email&utm_term=don&utm_content=20250725-AOTL-Tier1-EyesTX_&utm_campaign=EyesTX&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9FQS9FQTAxMy8xLzg5Mjk2IiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogIjk0MWIyMmI4LWEyNjktZjAxMS04ZGM5LTYwNDViZGE5ZDk2YiIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=6Sai0YjVtm1pHEDHE1NHAlx0K4d11FTly3BG7YfM3_w=)

**“White House Pushes Texas to Redistrict, Hoping to Blunt Democratic Gains”
— June 9, 2025**
White House officials have pushed for Texas legislators to pursue a “ruthless” gerrymander of its congressional map. That’s on top of the fact that Texas’s congressional map is already being sued for violating the Voting Rights Act.
Redrawing a map mid-decade in an effort to be unaccountable to the voters **sets a dangerous precedent** , one that bypasses the traditional redistricting process tied to new census data.
**Any president, political party, or elected official blatantly pushing to manipulate voting districts in pursuit of artificial power stands in direct conflict with American democratic values. **
[**That’s why All On The Line is on a mission to end gerrymandering — because it silences the will of the people. We deserve accountable, responsive elected leaders. For one, Texas’s special legislative session started on July 21st, and a new partisan gerrymander — even more egregious than the one already on the books in the Lone Star State — is on the agenda. Remember this?: = “White House Pushes Texas to Redistrict, Hoping to Blunt Democratic Gains” — June 9, 2025 White House officials have pushed for Texas legislators to pursue a “ruthless” gerrymander of its congressional map. That’s on top of the fact that Texas’s congressional map is already being sued for violating the Voting Rights Act. Redrawing a map mid-decade in an effort to be unaccountable to the voters sets a dangerous precedent , one that bypasses the traditional redistricting process tied to new census data. Any president, political party, or elected official blatantly pushing to manipulate voting districts in pursuit of artificial power stands in direct conflict with American democratic values. = = Peter, Texas Governor Greg Abbott has succumbed to pressure from the White House by adding redistricting to the agenda, and officials may very well follow suit by voting to pass it. Because no matter the cost to voters, maintaining power is the priority for far-right extremists. And for that very reason, we need to be on high alert and ready to mobilize fair maps supporters in this fight. ## Bret Stephens Whitewashes Genocide
**STEPHENS: It may seem harsh to say, but there is a glaring dissonance to the charge that Israel is committing genocide in Gaza. To wit: If the Israeli government 's intentions and actions are truly genocidal -- if it is so malevolent that it is committed to the annihilation of Gazans -- why hasn't it been more methodical and vastly more deadly?**
Stephens already commits three ridiculous errors in his opening sentence.
First, he misrepresents the definition of genocide. The term _genocide_ was coined in 1944 by Polish Jewish Lawyer Ralph Lemkin. Lemkin's heroic groundwork led us to the now universally adopted definition of genocide as follows, as enshrined in [Article II of the Convention on the Prevention and Punishment of the Crime of Genocide](https://substack.com/redirect/3f7caa01-5da7-4d50-9947-80e6fef3ee68?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg):
> Any of the following acts committed with intent to destroy, in whole or in part, a national, ethnical, racial or religious group, as such:
> (a) Killing members of the group;
> (b) Causing serious bodily or mental harm to members of the group;
> (c) Deliberately inflicting on the group conditions of life calculated to bring about its physical destruction in whole or in part;
> (d) Imposing measures intended to prevent births within the group;
> (e) Forcibly transferring children of the group to another group.
Stephens hopes that his readers ignore that at the definition of genocide specifically rejects the idea that an act must reach a particular level of "methodical or vastness" before it can count as genocide. Instead, the definition quite specifically points to an act as genocide even if it only intends to destroy "part" of a national, ethnical, racial, or religious group. As I'll soon revisit, that is what is happening here.
Second, even if we were to accept Stephens made up definition of genocide, he never actually defines what he considers adequately "methodical and vastness" in how deadly such attacks _should_ have been on Palestinians to meet the threshold of genocide. In doing so, he again attempts to absolve Israel's actions.
Third, Stephens pretends that Israel hasn't _already_ "methodically and vastly" destroyed Gaza. At the same time, the Islamic State fighters have used masses of civilians as human shields, and have been indiscriminate about sniper and mortar fire. This fight, carried out over nine months, had broad bipartisan and international support. By some estimates, it left . I don't recall any campus protests. What Iraq has to do with Israel committing genocide of Palestinians is anyone's guess. But for Stephens to rightly condemn ISIS for using human shields, but defend Israel's systemic use of human shields, shows he doesn't actually care about the war crime, he only cares about defending Israel despite its war crimes. Moreover, there were extensive and sustained nationwide college protests against the United States illegally bombing Iraq. Is Stephens' contention that because every single bombing wasn't protested to the same extent that students are protesting genocide of Palestinians, somehow they aren't valid? These are the straws Stephens is grasping at. STEPHENS: Some readers may say that even if the war in Gaza isn 't genocide, it has gone on too long and needs to end. That's a fair point of view, shared by . Yes, it's gone on for at least 58 years since 1967, before Stephens was even born. Yet at no point has Stephens ever called for an end to this military occupation of Palestine. In other places, he's defended the occupation . For some reason I cannot imagine Stephens would be happy for a foreign military to violently enter his property, kick him and his family out of their homes, and then force him to silently suffer the indignity--yet that's what he expects out of Palestinians suffering illegal military occupation by Israel. If you 're finding value in this analysis, join us as a free or paid subscriber. STEPHENS: So why does the argument over the word "genocide" matter? Two reasons. First, while some pundits and scholars may sincerely believe the genocide charge, it is also used by and to equate modern Israel with Nazi Germany. The effect is to license a new wave of Jew hatred. Ironically, Stephens himself makes the comparison between modern Israel with Nazi Germany when he claims that whatever Israel is doing, it isn't what the Nazis did at the Wannsee conference. Moreover, as is his classic strategy when he doesn't have an argument, Stephens glazes over the facts--in this case, the extensive list of who has recognized this as genocide. It is not just "some pundits and scholars," as he asserts. It is the global consensus. This affirmation of genocide is a view shared by Amnesty International, The International Court of Justice, the UN Special rapporteur on Palestine, and numerous Israeli scholars including globally recognized Israeli Jewish Holocaust scholar Omer Bartov who : My inescapable conclusion has become that Israel is committing genocide against the Palestinian people. I have been teaching classes on genocide for a quarter of a century. I can recognize one when I see one. Here is a non-comprehensive list of the , ethnic cleansing, and war crimes--including testimonies from Israeli scholars including a former Israeli prime minister, defense ministers, and lawyers. Stephens would have us believe that Israeli and Jewish scholars are engaging in "Jew hatred," a shameless and inexcusable position to hold. Stephens continues. STEPHENS: Second, if genocide -- a word that was coined only in the 1940s -- is to retain its status as a uniquely horrific crime, then the term can't be promiscuously applied to any military situation we don't like. Wars are awful enough. But the abuse of the term "genocide" runs the risk of ultimately blinding us to real ones when they unfold. Earlier Stephens argues it wasn't genocide when Germany was indiscriminately bombed, and now he points out he knows full well that the word did not even exist when Germany was bombed. Once again, he shows his overt contradictions. Moreover, Germany wasn't bombed due to their ethnicity, they were bombed because Hitler was invading foreign nations, rounding up Jews, Romas, gay people, and disabled people into concentration and death camps, and actively waging war for world domination. Thus, the comparison also falls apart because the Palestinian people are doing none of those things. Finally, no one is "promiscuously" applying genocide to any military situation we don't like. The international consensus that this is genocide is due to application of the actual definition of genocide--no matter how much Stephens attempts to whitewash it. STEPHENS: The war in Gaza should be brought to an end in a way that ensures it is never repeated. To call it a genocide does nothing to advance that aim, except to dilute the meaning of a word we cannot afford to cheapen. Stephens concludes his OpEd with this empty platitude, calling for an end to the siege on Gaza while ignoring the culprits perpetuating it--namely Netanyahu, Trump, and their ilk. Perhaps the main reason Bret Stephens ignores the genocide happening right before his eyes, is because he refuses to grapple with the facts. As a journalist, he should cite facts to make his argument--even in an Opinion Editorial--but instead he cites his feelings, his assumptions, and his beliefs, seemingly all of which are at odds with demonstrable and observable facts. This is not journalism. It's propaganda. And it's deadly. Throughout his diatribe, Stephens never acknowledges what would bring an actual end to the atrocity in Gaza. He never acknowledges the ceasefires Netanyahu continues to break, or the binding UN resolutions Israel continues to violate, or the Israeli military targeting of civilians, or the Israeli military burning children alive, or the Israeli military shooting people seeking aid, or the Israeli military raping inmates, or the , or Israel's . No, in Stephens world, the year prior to 10/7 was not the deadliest year on record of the Israeli military killing more than 250 Palestinian civilians in the West Bank, including nearly 50 children (‪). In Stephens cruel world, 60,000+ civilians are justifiably murdered because of 10/7, and even if not, it's just too few deaths to be recognized as genocide anyway. As Palestinian-Canadian international lawyer Diana Buttu states, to people like Bret Stephens, "Nothing justifies 10/7, but 10/7 justifies everything." In Stephens world, "from the river to the sea" is a statement of genocide, but "We will wipe Gaza from the face of the Earth" followed by more bombing than was conducted during World War 2 is not. It is clear that Bret Stephens lives in an alternate reality where up is down and right is wrong, and the cost associated is our basic humanity. Conclusion History has no patience for those who enable atrocities under the guise of journalism. Bret Stephens isn't offering analysis--he's laundering genocide. He's twisting definitions, ignoring international law, and erasing the lived reality of Palestinians to shield a government from accountability. But genocide doesn't require his approval to be real. The mass graves are real. The starvation is real. The charred bodies of children are real. The destroyed hospitals are real. The destroyed mosques are real. The destroyed churches are real. And no amount of New York Times OpEd spin can wash the oceans of Palestinian blood from this truth. The New York Times once downplayed the Holocaust. Today, they're repeating that shameful legacy in real time. And just like then, silence is complicity. So yes, Bret Stephens, whether you want to face facts or not, the Israeli government is committing genocide of the Palestinian people. And rather than serve as water carriers for war criminals, you should serve as an actual representative of the Fourth Estate and hold the powerful accountable. But the choice is yours to stay on the wrong side of history, or join humanity on the right side. None the less, I'll close with this final point that Bret Stephens should remember: Nuremberg didn't only try those who dropped the bombs--but also those who justified them. The week of Independence Day, the U.S. Senate took on the tall order of passing President Trump’s sweeping domestic policy package – the One Big Beautiful Bill. After more than 26 hours of voting, the Senate passed the bill, which was then sent to the House of Representatives for final passage. On July 4, Trump signed it into law.

Needless to say, it was a busy – but very rewarding – week.

There’s been a lot of national conversation about how transformational this bill is. But let’s talk about what it means for Alabama.

U.S. Senator Katie Britt (R-Montgomery) is expressing continued confidence that the U.S. Space Command headquarters will be relocated to Huntsville after years of political controversy and bureaucratic delays.
